control.title: Digital Identity Risk Management - RP Process Implementation

part.name: statement
part.p: Federal RPs SHALL implement the DIRM process for all online services.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if all online services of the Federal RP are identified and ensure the DIRM process is implemented for those online services.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine DIRM policy to determine that it is intended to cover all organizational applications. If available, review the list of online services to ensure all services are identified and that DIRM documentation for each online service exists.

part.name: guidance
part.p: For relying parties, the intent of [the DIRM] process is to determine the assurance levels and any tailoring required to protect all online services and the applications, transactions, and systems that comprise or are impacted by those services. This directly contributes to the selection, development, and procurement of CSP services.

control.title: Digital Identity Risk Management - CSP/IdP Communication of Normative Deviations

part.name: statement
part.p: Whenever a service offering deviates from normative guidance, those deviations SHALL be clearly communicated to the RPs that utilize the service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the CSP/IdP has a documented process for communicating when their services deviate from the established normative guidance of the applicable NIST SP 900-63 requirements.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the CSP/IdP policy for communicating deviations from normative guidance.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview relying party customers to confirm they are familiar with the policy and process for communication and determine if the process is being used.

part.name: guidance
part.p: For credential service providers and identity providers, the intent of [the DIRM] process is to design service offerings that meet the requirements of the defined assurance levels, continuously guard against compromises to the identity system, and meet the needs of RPs.

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, organizations SHALL execute and document each step and complete and document the normative mandates and outcomes of each step, regardless of any organization-specific processes or tools used in the overall DIRM process.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that each step of the DIRM process is executed and documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM process documentation to ensure the outcomes of each step are completed as applicable.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This requirement is agnostic to any organization-specific processes or tools used in the overall DIRM process.(Ref. Sec. 3.0 #A)

control.title: Define Online Services - Mission and Business

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL develop a description of the online service that includes the organizational mission and business objectives supported by the online service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the online service has been developed that includes the organizational mission and business objectives that are supported by the online service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it includes a description of its organizational mission and business objectives.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this initial step is to establish a common understanding of the online service's context and functionality, which is essential for informing the subsequent risk assessment steps of the DIRM process.

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL develop a description of the online service that includes the mission and business partner dependencies associated with the online service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the online service has been developed that includes the mission and business partner dependencies associated with the online service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it includes its associated mission and business partner dependencies.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this initial step is to establish a common understanding of the online service's context and functionality, which is essential for informing the subsequent risk assessment steps of the DIRM process.

control.title: Define Online Services - Legal, Regulatory, Contractual

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL develop a description of the online service that includes legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements, including privacy obligations that apply to the online service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the online service has been developed that includes the legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements, including obligations that apply to the online service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it includes its legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements, including obligations that apply to the online service.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this initial step is to establish a common understanding of the online service's context and functionality, which is essential for informing the subsequent risk assessment steps of the DIRM process.

control.title: Define Online Services - Functionality and Data Processing

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL develop a description of the online service that includes the functionality of the online service and the data that it is expected to process.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the online service has been developed that includes the functionality of the online service and the data that it is expected to process.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it includes its functionality and the data that it is expected to process.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this initial step is to establish a common understanding of the online service's context and functionality, which is essential for informing the subsequent risk assessment steps of the DIRM process.

control.title: Define Online Services - User Groups Transactions & Access Privileges

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL develop a description of the online service that includes user groups that need to have access to the online service as well as the types of online transactions and access privileges available to each user group.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the online service has been developed that includes the user groups that need to have access to the online service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it identifies user groups and the transaction types and access privileges associated with each group.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this initial step is to establish a common understanding of the online service's context and functionality, which is essential for informing the subsequent risk assessment steps of the DIRM process.
The set of entities includes users of the online service, organizations, and populations served.
It is crucial to differentiate between user groups and impacted entities.
(a) User groups are users who are partitioned based on the specific functionality or access privileges offered to them (e.g., citizens checking tax status vs. tax preparers filing returns).

(b) Impacted entities include everyone who could face negative consequences if the identity system fails. This group includes members of the user groups but also potentially those who never directly use the system.

control.title: Define Online Services - Impacted Entities and Business Processes

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL develop a description of the online service that includes the set of entities (to include users of the online service, organizations, and populations served) that will be impacted by the online service and the broader business process of which it is a part.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the online service has been developed that includes the set of entities that will be impacted by the online service and the broader business process of which it is a part.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it includes the set of entities that will be impacted by the online service and the broader business process of which it is a part.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this initial step is to establish a common understanding of the online service's context and functionality, which is essential for informing the subsequent risk assessment steps of the DIRM process. The set of entities includes users of the online service, organizations, and populations served.

control.title: Define Online Services - Previous Assessment Results and Technologies

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL develop a description of the online service that includes the results of any preexisting DIRM assessments (as an input) and the current state of any preexisting identity technologies (i.e., proofing, authentication, or federation).

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the online service has been developed that includes the results of any preexisting DIRM assessments and the current state of any preexisting identity technologies.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it includes the results of any preexisting DIRM assessments and/or a description of the current state of any preexisting identity technologies.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this initial step is to establish a common understanding of the online service's context and functionality, which is essential for informing the subsequent risk assessment steps of the DIRM process.

control.title: Define Online Services - Identity Evidence Availability

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL develop a description of the online service that includes the estimated availability of the types of identity evidence required for identity proofing across all user groups served.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the online service has been developed that includes the estimated availability of the types of identity evidence required for identity proofing across all user groups served.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it includes the estimated availability of the types of identity evidence required for identity proofing across all user groups served.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this initial step is to establish a common understanding of the online service's context and functionality, which is essential for informing the subsequent risk assessment steps of the DIRM process.

control.title: Define Online Services - Impact Assessment Scope - Users and Organization

part.name: statement
part.p: The scope of impact assessments SHALL include individuals who use the online service as well as the organization itself.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the scope of impact assessments includes impacts to individuals who use the online service and impacts to the organization.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure the impact assessments address impacts to the individuals who use the online service and impacts to the organization.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Note: "online application" is the same as "online service".

control.title: Define Online Services - Impact Assessment Scope - Entities included in Mission and Business Needs

part.name: statement
part.p: The scope of impact assessments for organizations SHALL identify other entities (e.g., mission partners, communities, and those identified in [SP800-30]) that need to be specifically included based on mission and business needs.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the scope of impact assessments for organizations identify other entities that need to be specifically included based on mission and business needs.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure the impact assessments address mission partners and other external organizations that may be impacted by the online service.

part.name: guidance
part.p: DOS-3 deals with user groups.

control.title: Define Online Services - Impact Assessment Scope - Impacted Entities

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, organizations SHALL document all impacted entities (both internal and external to the organization) when conducting their impact assessments.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the scope of impact assessments for organizations identify all internal and external impacted entities.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM documentation for each online service to ensure it includes a description of the scope of impact assessments for organizations that identifies all internal and external impacted entities.

part.name: guidance
part.p: DOS-4 deals with impacted entities.

control.title: Impact Assessment - Potential Harms for Impact Categories

part.name: statement
part.p: The impact assessment SHALL include a set of impact categories and the potential harms for each impact category.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that the impact assessment includes a set of impact categories and the potential harms for each impact category.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM impact assessment documentation to establish that the impact assessment includes a set of impact categories and the potential harms for each impact category.

control.title: Impact Assessment - Levels of Impact Identification

part.name: statement
part.p: The impact assessment SHALL include identifying the levels of impact.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that the impact assessment includes the levels of impact.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM impact assessment documentation to establish that the impact assessment includes the levels of impact.

control.title: Impact Assessment - Levels of Impact - User Groups

part.name: statement
part.p: The impact assessment SHALL include assessing the level of impact for each user group.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that the impact assessment includes an assessment of the level of impact for each user group.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM impact assessment documentation to establish that the impact assessment includes an assessment for the level of impact for each user group.

control.title: Impact Assessment - Levels of Impact - Transactions

part.name: statement
part.p: The level of impact for each user group identified in Sec. 3.1 SHALL be considered separately based on the transactions available to that user group.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the levels of impact for each user group is considered separately based on the transactions available to that user group.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM impact assessment documentation to establish that the levels of impact for each user group is considered separately based on the transactions available to that user group.

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, organizations SHALL include the following impact categories in their impact assessments:
(a) Degradation of mission delivery.
(b) Damage to trust, standing, or reputation.
(c) Unauthorized access to information.
(d) Financial loss or liability.
(e) Loss of life or danger to human safety, human health, or environmental health.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the impact categories in the impact assessments include degradation of mission delivery, damage to trust, standing, or reputation, unauthorized access to information, financial loss or liability, and loss of life or danger to human safety, human health, or environmental health.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM impact assessment documentation to establish that the impact categories include degradation of mission delivery, damage to trust, standing, or reputation, unauthorized access to information, financial loss or liability, and loss of life or danger to human safety, human health, or environmental health.

part.name: statement
part.p: Each impact category SHALL be documented and consistently applied when implementing the DIRM process across different online services offered by the organization.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if, for each online service offered by the organization, each impact category is documented and applied as part of the DIRM process.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM impact assessment documentation to establish that, for each online service, each impact category is documented and applied.

part.name: statement
part.p: For each impact category, organizations SHALL consider potential harms for each of the impacted entities identified in Sec. 3.1

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if potential harms are identified for each impact category and each of the impacted entities.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the organization's DIRM impact assessment documentation to establish that potential harms are identified for each impact category and each of the impacted entities.

control.title: Potential Impact Levels - Threshold Development, Examples, and Documentation

part.name: statement
part.p: To provide a more objective basis for impact level assignments, organizations SHOULD develop thresholds and examples for the impact levels for each impact category. Where this is done, particularly with specifically defined quantifiable values, these thresholds SHALL be documented and used consistently in the DIRM assessments across an organization to allow for a common understanding of risks.

part.name: objective
part.p: PIL-1Obj1: Determine if thresholds and examples for the impact levels for each impact category have been developed. (0ptional) PIL-1Obj2: Determine if PIL-1Obj1 is documented and used consistently in the DIRM assessments. (conditional)

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM impact assessment documentation to verify that they are documented, including any specifically defined quantifiable values, and look for evidence of consistent use in the DIRM assessments.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: thresholds and examples for the impact levels were developed.

control.title: Impact Analysis - Impacts from Unauthorized Access

part.name: statement
part.p: The impact analysis SHALL consider the level of impact for each impact category for each type of impacted entity if an intruder obtains unauthorized access as a member of each user group.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the impact analysis considers the level of impact resulting from unauthorized access, for each impact category for each type of impacted entity.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the analysis of the organization's DIRM impact assessment to establish that it considers impacts from unauthorized access for each type of impacted entity,

part.name: statement
part.p: The impact analysis SHALL be performed for each user group that has access to the online service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the impact analysis is performed for each user group that has access to the online service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation for the impact analyses performed to determine that one exists for each user group that has access to the online service.

part.name: statement
part.p: The output of this impact analysis is a set of impact levels for each user group that SHALL be documented for further analysis in accordance with Sec. 3.4.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the output of the impact analysis includes a documented set of impact levels.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the output of the impact analysis to verify that it includes a documented set of impact levels.

control.title: Combined Impact - Overall Impact Level and Application

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL document the approach they use to combine their impact assessment into an overall impact level for each of their defined user groups and SHALL apply it consistently across all of its online services.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the approach used to combine the impact assessment into an overall impact level for each defined user group has been documented.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the approach used to combine the impact assessment into an overall impact level for each defined user group is applied consistently across all online services.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM process documentation to ensure that the approach used to combine the impact assessment into an overall impact level for each defined user group has been documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the person/people responsible for implementing this approach to ensure they understand the approach and are implementing it consistently.

part.name: statement
part.p: At the conclusion of the combinatorial analysis, organizations SHALL document the impact for each user group.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the overall impact levels for each user group have been documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the completed combined impact assessments to ensure the approach and results for each user group have been documented.

part.name: statement
part.p: The RP SHALL identify the types of assurance levels that apply to their online service from the following:
(a) IAL: The robustness of the identity proofing process to determine the identity of an individual. The IAL is selected to mitigate risks that result from potential identity proofing failures.

(b) AAL: The robustness of the authentication process itself and the binding between an authenticator and a specific individual's identifier. The AAL is selected to mitigate risks that result from potential authentication failures.

(c) FAL: The robustness of the federation process used to communicate authentication and attribute information to an RP from an IdP. The FAL is selected to mitigate risks that result from potential federation failures.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the online service needs an IAL, AAL, or FAL.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documented needs of the identity service, the results of the DIRM documentation completed to date, and the IAL requirements from 800-63A, to determine if identity proofing is necessary.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documented needs of the identity service, the results of the DIRM documentation completed to date, and the IAL requirements from 800-63B, to determine if authentication is needed.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documented needs of the identity service, the results of the DIRM documentation completed to date, and the IAL requirements from 800-63C, to determine if federation is needed.

control.title: Initial Assurance Level Selection - Process and Governance Documentation

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL develop and document a process and governance model for selecting initial assurance levels and controls based on the potential impacts of failures in the digital identity system.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the process and governance model for selecting initial assurance levels and controls has been developed based on the potential impacts of failures in the digital identity system and has been documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM documentation to verify that the process and governance model for selecting initial assurance levels and controls has been developed and documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the process and governance model documentation and identify the potential impacts of failures that the process and governance model were based on.

part.name: statement
part.p: The organization SHALL document whether identity proofing is required for their application.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the question of whether identity proofing is required for the online service has been documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the online service documentation to verify that the results of the analysis to determine the need for identity proofing has been documented.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This documents the results of control AL-1.

part.name: statement
part.p: If identity proofing is required for their application, the organization SHALL select an initial IAL for each user group based on the effective impact level determination from Sec. 3.2.4.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if an initial IAL for each user group was determined and is based on the impact level determination (see CIL requirements)

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documentation to verify that the initial IAL has been determined for each user group and is based on the effective impact level determination (See CIL controls).

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: the online service requires identity proofing for their user groups. See AL-1. If identity proofing is required, see CIL controls for impact levels.

part.name: statement
part.p: The organization SHALL document whether authentication is required for their application.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the question of whether authentication is required for the online service has been documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the online service documentation to verify that the results of the analysis to determine the need for authentication has been documented.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This documents the results of requirement AL-1.

part.name: statement
part.p: If authentication is required for their application, the organization SHALL select an initial AAL for each user group based on the effective impact level determination from Sec. 3.2.4.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if an initial AAL for each user group was determined and is based on the impact level determination (see CIL requirements)

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documentation to verify that the initial AAL has been determined for each user group and is based on the effective impact level determination (See CIL controls).

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: the online service requires authentication. See AL-1. If authentication is required, see CIL controls for impact levels.

part.name: statement
part.p: The organization SHALL document whether federation is required for their application.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the question of whether federation is required for the online service has been documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the online service documentation to verify that the results of the analysis to determine the need for federation has been documented.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This documents the results of the FAL assessment in control AL-1. Assessment is required when: the organization will use federation.

part.name: statement
part.p: If federation is required for their application, the organization SHALL select an initial FAL for each user group based on the effective impact level determination from Sec. 3.2.4.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if an initial FAL for each user group was determined and is based on the impact level determination (see CIL requirements)

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documentation to verify that the initial FAL has been determined for each user group and is based on the effective impact level determination (See CIL controls).

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: the online service requires federation. See AL-1. If federation will be used, see CIL controls for impact levels.

control.title: Initial FAL - FAL2 or FAL3 Assessment

part.name: statement
part.p: For online services that are assessed to be high impact, organizations SHALL conduct a further assessment to evaluate the risk of a compromised IdP to determine whether FAL2 or FAL3 is more appropriate for their use case.

part.name: objective
part.p: If the online service is "high impact," determine if further assessment has been done to evaluate the risk of a compromised IdP and if FAL2 or FAL3 is more appropriate.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documentation for additional assessments that evaluate if FAL2 or FAL3 is more appropriate.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Dependent on the results from controls AL-1 and IFAL-1a. Assessment is required when: the online service is assessed to be "high-impact."

part.name: statement
part.p: Using the initial xALs selected in Sec. 3.3.3, the organization SHALL identify the applicable baseline controls for each user group for the Initial IAL and related technical and process controls from [SP800-63A].

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the applicable baseline controls for the initial IAL and related technical and process controls have been identified for each user group in alignment with SP 800-63A.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the initial IAL baseline controls and related technical and process controls to determine that they are in alignment with SP 800-63A for each user group.

part.name: guidance
part.p: See IIAL controls.

part.name: statement
part.p: Using the initial xALs selected in Sec. 3.3.3, the organization SHALL identify the applicable baseline controls for each user group for the Initial AAL and related technical and process controls from [SP800-63B].

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the applicable baseline controls for the initial AAL and related technical and process controls have been identified for each user group in alignment with SP 800-63B.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the initial AAL baseline controls and related technical and process controls to determine that they are in alignment with SP 800-63B for each user group.

part.name: guidance
part.p: See IAAL controls.

part.name: statement
part.p: Using the initial xALs selected in Sec. 3.3.3, the organization SHALL identify the applicable baseline controls for each user group for the Initial FAL and related technical and process controls from [SP800-63C].

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the applicable baseline controls for the initial FAL and related technical and process controls have been identified for each user group in alignment with SP 800-63C.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the initial FAL baseline controls and related technical and process controls to determine that they are in alignment with SP 800-63C for each user group

part.name: guidance
part.p: See IFAL controls.

part.name: statement
part.p: Within the tailoring step, organizations SHALL focus on impacts to mission delivery due to the implementation of identity management controls.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the impacts to mission delivery are used as a focus for the tailoring step.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring documentation to ensure impacts to mission are used as a focus.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Impacts include the possibility of legitimate users who are unable to access desired online services or experience sufficient friction or frustration with the identity system (and technology selection) that they abandon attempts to access the online service.(Ref. Sec. 3.4 A)

part.name: statement
part.p: As a part of the tailoring process, organizations SHALL review the Digital Identity Acceptance Statements (DIAS) and practice statements from CSPs and IdPs that they use or intend to use.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the DIAS and practice statements from CSPs and IdPs have been reviewed as part of the tailoring process.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the person/team responsible for completing the tailoring step to ensure they reviewed the DIAS and practice statements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL also conduct their own analysis to ensure that their specific mission and the communities being served by the online service are given due consideration for tailoring purposes.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the tailoring process includes organizations' own analysis to ensure that their mission and communities served by the online services are given due consideration.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring documentation to ensure analysis was done, and due consideration given, to the organization specific mission and the communities being served by the online service.

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL establish and document their xAL tailoring process.

part.name: objective
part.p: (1) Determine if the xAL tailoring process has been documented.
(2) Determine if the xAL tailoring process has been implemented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring process documentation for each xAL to verify its existence and completeness.

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, [the tailoring] process SHALL follow a documented governance approach to allow for decision-making.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the tailoring process follows a documented governance approach that allows for decision-making.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring process documentation for information on the governance approach that allows for decision-making.

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, [the tailoring] process SHALL document all decisions in the tailoring process (see Sec. 3.4.4).

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the tailoring process documents all decisions made during the tailoring process.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring process documentation to determine that all decisions made during the tailoring process have been documented.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Examples of decisions include the assessed xALs, modified xALs, and supplemental and compensating controls in the Digital Identity Acceptance Statement

control.title: Tailor Assurance Levels - Document Risk-Based Decisions

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, the [tailoring] process SHALL justify and document all risk-based decisions or modifications to the initially assessed xALs in the Digital Identity Acceptance Statement (DIAS) (see Sec. 3.4.4).

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the tailoring process justifies and documents all risk-based decisions or modifications to the initially selected xALs in the DIAS.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring process documentation to ensure justifications are included in the documented risk-based decisions or modifications that apply to the initially selected xALs in the DIAS.

control.title: Privacy, Customer Experience, Threat Resistance - Identify Impacts

part.name: statement
part.p: When progressing from the initial assurance level selection in [the Baseline Controls requirements] (Sec. 3.3.4) to the final xAL selection and implementation, organizations SHALL conduct detailed assessments of the controls defined for the initially selected xALs to identify potential impacts in the operational environment.

part.name: objective
part.p: As part of the selection of the final xALs, determine if a detailed assessment of the initial xAL controls was conducted and identified potential impacts in the operational environment.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM documentation indicating the final xAL selection to ensure it includes a detailed assessment of the initial xAL controls and identifies potential impacts in the operational environment.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the person(s) responsible for conducting the assessment of the initial xAL controls for how they identified the potential impacts in the operational environment.

control.title: Privacy, Customer Experience, Threat Resistance - Privacy Impact Assessment

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, organizations SHALL assess the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to Privacy - Identify unintended consequences to the privacy of individuals who will be subject to the controls at an assessed xAL and of individuals affected by organizational or third-party practices related to the establishment, management, or federation of a digital identity. A privacy assessment SHOULD leverage an existing Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA) or Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) as inputs during the privacy assessment process.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the organization assessed the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to privacy.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM documentation indicating the final xAL selection to ensure it includes an assessment of the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to privacy.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the person(s) responsible for assessing the impacts and potential consequences related to privacy to determine if they leveraged a PTA or PIA as part of their process. (optional)

part.name: guidance
part.p: As the goal of the privacy assessment is to identify privacy risks that arise from the initial assurance level selection, additional assessments and evaluations that are specific to the baseline controls for the assurance levels may be required for the underlying information system. Leveraging an existing PTA or PIA is recommended.

control.title: Privacy, Customer Experience, Threat Resistance - Customer Experience Impact Assessment

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, organizations SHALL assess the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to Customer Experience - Determine whether implementation of the initial assurance levels may create substantial or unacceptable barriers to individuals seeking to access services. Customer experience assessments SHALL consider impacts that result from the identity management controls to ensure that they do not cause undue burdens, frustrations, or frictions for individuals and that there are pathways to provide service to users of all capabilities, resources, technology access, and economic statuses.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the organization assessed the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to customer experience.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM documentation indicating the final xAL selection to ensure it includes an assessment of the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to customer experience, such as undue burdens, frustrations, or frictions for individuals, as well as pathways to provide service to users of all capabilities, resources, technology access, and economic statuses.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Determine whether implementation of the initial assurance levels may create substantial or unacceptable barriers to individuals seeking to access services.

control.title: Privacy, Customer Experience, Threat Resistance - Threat Resistance Impact Assessment

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, organizations SHALL assess the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to Threat Resistance - Determine whether the defined assurance level and related controls will address specific threats to the online service based on the operational environment, its threat actors, and known tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs). Threat assessments SHALL consider specific known and potential threats, threat actors, and TTPs within the implementation environment for the identity management functions.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the organization assessed the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to threat resistance.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM documentation indicating the final xAL selection to ensure there is an assessment of the impacts and potential unintended consequences related to threat resistance showing that the defined assurance level and related controls address: 1) specific threats to the online service based on the operation environment, 2) the threat actors of those specific threats and known TTPs.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the person(s) responsible for assessing the impacts and potential consequences related to privacy to determine if and how they considered specific known and potential threats, threat actors, and TTPs within the implementation environment for the identity management functions.

part.name: guidance
part.p: For example, certain benefits programs may be more subject to familial threats or collusion. Based on their assessments, organizations MAY implement supplemental controls specific to the communities served by their online service. Conversely, organizations MAY tailor their assessed xAL down or modify their baseline controls if their threat assessment indicates that a reduced threat posture is appropriate based on their environment.

control.title: Privacy, Customer Experience, Threat Resistance - Compensating and Supplemental Controls

part.name: statement
part.p: All assessments applied during the tailoring phase SHALL be extended to any compensating or supplemental controls, as defined in Sec. 3.4.2 and Sec. 3.4.3.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if all assessments applied during the tailoring phase were extended to any identified compensating or supplemental controls.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIRM documentation indicating the final xAL selection to ensure all assessments applied during the tailoring phase were extended to any compensating or supplemental controls identified in ICC-1 and ISC-1.

part.name: guidance
part.p: A compensating control is a management, operational, or technical control employed by an organization in lieu of a normative control (i.e., SHALL statements) in the defined xALs. (Ref. Sec. 3.4.2. A) The purpose of this requirement is to allow the RP to assess and determine the acceptability of the compensating controls for their use cases.(Ref. Sec. 3.4.2. C) Assessment is required when: compensating controls are implemented. Per section 3.4.2, "Organizations MAY choose to implement a compensating control if they are unable to implement a baseline control or when a risk assessment indicates that a compensating control sufficiently mitigates risk in alignment with organizational risk tolerance. This control MAY be a modification to the normative statements defined in these guidelines or MAY be applied elsewhere in an online service, digital transaction, or service life cycle."

control.title: Privacy, Customer Experience, Threat Resistance - Cost-based Decision Documentation

part.name: statement
part.p: Any cost-based decisions that result in modifications to assessed xALs or baseline controls SHALL be documented in the Digital Identity Acceptance Statement (see Sec. 3.4.4).

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if cost-based decisions that result in modification to assessed xALs or baseline controls are documented in the Digital Identity Acceptance Statement (DIAS).

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIAS to ensure cost-based decisions that resulted in modification to the assessed xALs or baseline controls are documented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Where compensating controls are implemented, organizations SHALL document the compensating control, the rationale for the deviation, comparability of the chosen alternative, and any resulting residual risks.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if implemented compensating controls are documented, including the rationale for the deviation, comparability of the chosen alternative, and any resulting residual risks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring documentation to ensure implemented compensating controls are fully documented, including the rationale for the deviation, comparability of the chosen alternative, and any resulting residual risks.

part.name: guidance
part.p: A compensating control is a management, operational, or technical control employed by an organization in lieu of a normative control (i.e., SHALL statements) in the defined xALs. (Ref. Sec. 3.4.2. A) The purpose of this requirement is to allow the RP to assess and determine the acceptability of the compensating controls for their use cases.(Ref. Sec. 3.4.2. C) Assessment is required when: compensating controls are implemented. Per section 3.4.2, "Organizations MAY choose to implement a compensating control if they are unable to implement a baseline control or when a risk assessment indicates that a compensating control sufficiently mitigates risk in alignment with organizational risk tolerance. This control MAY be a modification to the normative statements defined in these guidelines or MAY be applied elsewhere in an online service, digital transaction, or service life cycle."

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs and IdPs that implement compensating controls SHALL communicate this information to all potential RPs prior to integration.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if CSPs and IdPs that implement compensating controls have communicated this information to all potential RPs prior to integration.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine CSP/IdP communications with all RPs and potential RPs to ensure the information regarding the implementation of those compensating controls was done prior to their integration.

part.name: guidance
part.p: A compensating control is a management, operational, or technical control employed by an organization in lieu of a normative control (i.e., SHALL statements) in the defined xALs. (Ref. Sec. 3.4.2. A) The purpose of this requirement is to allow the RP to assess and determine the acceptability of the compensating controls for their use cases.(Ref. Sec. 3.4.2. C) Assessment is required when: compensating controls are implemented. Per section 3.4.2, "Organizations MAY choose to implement a compensating control if they are unable to implement a baseline control or when a risk assessment indicates that a compensating control sufficiently mitigates risk in alignment with organizational risk tolerance. This control MAY be a modification to the normative statements defined in these guidelines or MAY be applied elsewhere in an online service, digital transaction, or service life cycle."

part.name: statement
part.p: Any supplemental controls SHALL be assessed for impacts based on the same factors used to tailor the organization's assurance level.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if supplemental controls are assessed for impacts based on the same factors used to tailor the organization's assurance level.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring documentation to ensure any implemented supplemental controls have been assessed for impacts based on the same factors used to tailor the initial xALs. See TAL and PCT requirements.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: supplemental controls are identified and implemented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Any supplemental controls SHALL be documented.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if supplemental controls are documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the tailoring documentation to ensure implemented supplemental controls are fully documented.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: supplemental controls are identified and implemented.

control.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement - Documentation - Managed Online Services

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL develop a Digital Identity Acceptance Statement (DIAS) to document the results of the DIRM process for each online service managed by the organization.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a DIAS was developed that documents the results of the DIRM process for each online service managed by the organization.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIAS to verify documentation of the DIRM process results for each online service managed by the organization.

part.name: guidance
part.p: See DIRM-1.

control.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement - Documentation - External Online Services

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL develop a Digital Identity Acceptance Statement (DIAS) to document the results of the DIRM process for each external online service used to support the mission of the organization.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a DIAS was developed that documents the results of the DIRM process for each external online service used to support the mission of the organization.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIAS to verify documentation of the DIRM process results for each external online service used to support the mission of the organization.

part.name: guidance
part.p: External online services include software-as-a-service offerings (e.g., social media platforms, email services, online marketing services). (Ref. Sec. 3.4.4.A) See DIRM-1

control.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement - Incorporating External DIAS Information

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs who intend to use a particular CSP/IdP SHALL review the latter's DIAS and incorporate relevant information into the organization's DIAS for each online service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the RP reviewed the CSP/IdP's DIAS and incorporated relevant information into the RP's DIAS for each online service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine each RP online service's DIAS for relevant information from the DIAS of the CSP/IdP the RP intends to use.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: the CSP/IdP used by the RP has created a DIAS.

control.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement - Online Service DIAS contents

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL prepare a DIAS for their online service that includes, at a minimum:
(a) Initial impact assessment results; initially assessed xALs.
(b) Tailored xALs and rationale if the tailored xALs differs from the initially assessed xALs.
(c) All compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks.
(d) All supplemental controls.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the organization's online service DIAS includes, at a minimum, initial impact assessment results, initially assessed xALs, tailored xALs and rationale if the tailored xALs differs from the initially assessed xALs, all compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks, and all supplemental controls.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine each DIAS to ensure it includes the initial impact assessment results, initially assessed xALs, tailored xALs and rationale if the tailored xALs differs from the initially assessed xALs, all compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks, and all supplemental controls.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required for a CS{/IdP when: the CSP/IdP deviates from normative guidance and creates a DIAS.

control.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement - CSP DIAS Implementation

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs/IdPs SHALL implement the DIRM process and develop a DIAS for the services they offer if they deviate from the normative guidance in these guidelines, including when supplemental or compensating controls are added.

part.name: objective
part.p: For CSP/IdPs that deviate from normative guidance, determine if the CSP/IdP has implemented the DIRM process and developed a DIAS for the services they offer.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documentation to ensure the DIRM process was implemented and a DIAS developed for their offered services.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: the CSP/IdP deviates from normative guidance, including when supplemental or compensating controls are added. To complete a DIRM of their offered assurance levels and controls, CSPs/IdPs MAY base their assessment on anticipated or representative digital identity services that they wish to support.

control.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement - CSP DIAS Elements

part.name: statement
part.p: The DIAS prepared by a CSP SHALL include, at a minimum:
(a) Claimed xAL, related controls, and rationale for any deviations from normative guidance;
(b) All compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks; and
(c) All supplemental controls.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the CSP's DIAS includes the claimed xAL, related controls, and rationale for any deviations from normative guidance, all compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks, and all supplemental controls.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the CSP's DIAS to ensure it includes claimed xAL, related controls, and rationale for any deviations from normative guidance, all compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks, and all supplemental controls.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: the CSP/IdP has created a DIAS (see DIAS-4).

control.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement - Documentation of Relevant Inputs

part.name: statement
part.p: The DIRM process for external online services used by the organization SHALL consider relevant inputs from the provider of the service and document the results in a DIAS.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the DIRM process for external online services includes the results of inputs from the provider of the service are documented in a DIAS.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIAS containing the results of the DIRM process for external online services used by the organization includes and documents relevant inputs from the provider of the service.

part.name: guidance
part.p: CSP's trying to meet this requirement should coordinate with the RP for the documentation.

control.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement - External Online Services DIAS

part.name: statement
part.p: The DIAS prepared by the organization for external online services SHALL include, at a minimum:
(a) Assessed xAL, related controls, and rationale for any deviations from normative guidance;
(b) All compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks; and
(c) All supplemental controls.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the DIAS for external online services includes assessed xALs, related controls, and rationale for any deviations from normative guidance, all compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks, and all supplemental controls.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the DIAS prepared for each external online services to ensure they include assessed xALs, related controls, and rationale for any deviations from normative guidance, all compensating controls with their comparability or residual risks, and all supplemental controls.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: the CSP/IdP created a DIAS (see DIAS-4)

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL implement a continuous evaluation and improvement program that leverages input from end users who have interacted with the identity management system as well as performance metrics for the online service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the organization has implemented a continuous evaluation and improvement program that leverages input from end users who have interacted with the identity management system and performance metrics for the online service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation that describes the continuous evaluation and improvement program to ensure it leverages input from end users who have interacted with the identity management system.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation that describes the continuous evaluation and improvement program to ensure it leverages input from performance metrics for the online service.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of this control is to address the shifting environment in which they operate and more rapidly address service capability gaps.

part.name: statement
part.p: This program SHALL be documented, including the metrics that are collected, the sources of data required to enable performance evaluation, and the processes in place for taking timely actions based on the continuous improvement process.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the documentation includes:
(a) the metrics that are collected,
(b) the sources of data required to enable performance evaluation, and
(c) the processes in place for taking timely actions based on the continuous improvement process.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the continuous evaluation and improvement program documentation to ensure it includes all collected metrics.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the continuous evaluation and improvement program documentation to ensure it includes the sources of data required to enable performance evaluation.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the continuous evaluation and improvement program documentation to ensure it includes the processes in place for taking timely actions based on the continuous improvement process.

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL monitor the evolving threat landscape.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the organization is monitoring the evolving threat landscape.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the continuous evaluation and improvement program documentation to ensure it includes policies and procedures for monitoring the evolving threat landscape.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of monitoring the evolving threat landscape is to stay informed of the latest threats and fraud tactics.

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL regularly assess the effectiveness of current security measures and fraud detection capabilities against the latest threats and fraud tactics.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the organization regularly assesses the effectiveness of current security measures and fraud detection capabilities against the latest threats and fraud tactics.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the continuous evaluation and improvement program documentation (policy and logs) for evidence that the effectiveness of current security measures and fraud detection capabilities against the latest threats and fraud tactics is being assessed regularly.

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, evaluation inputs SHALL include:
(a) Integrated CSP, IdP, and authentication functions as well as validation, verification, and fraud management systems, as appropriate;
(b) Customer feedback mechanisms, such as complaint processes, helpdesk statistics, and other user feedback (e.g., surveys, interviews, or focus groups);
(c) Threat analysis, threat reporting, and threat intelligence feeds that are available;
(d) Fraud trends, fraud investigation results, and fraud metrics as available; and
(e) The results of ongoing customer experience assessments and privacy assessments.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the evaluation inputs include:
(a) Integrated CSP, IdP, and authentication functions as well as validation, verification, and fraud management systems, as appropriate;

(b) Customer feedback mechanisms, such as complaint processes, helpdesk statistics, and other user feedback (e.g., surveys, interviews, or focus groups); (c)Threat analysis, threat reporting, and threat intelligence feeds that are available;
(d) Fraud trends, fraud investigation results, and fraud metrics as available; and
(e) The results of ongoing customer experience assessments and privacy assessments.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the continuous evaluation and improvement program documentation evaluation inputs to ensure they include:
(a) Integrated CSP, IdP, and authentication functions as well as validation, verification, and fraud management systems, as appropriate;
(b) Customer feedback mechanisms, such as complaint processes, helpdesk statistics, and other user feedback (e.g., surveys, interviews, or focus groups);
(c) Threat analysis, threat reporting, and threat intelligence feeds that are available; (d)Fraud trends, fraud investigation results, and fraud metrics as available; and
(e) The results of ongoing customer experience assessments and privacy assessments.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test the continuous evaluation and improvement program to ensure it can use all the following evaluation inputs:
(a) Integrated CSP, IdP, and authentication functions as well as validation, verification, and fraud management systems, as appropriate;
(b) Customer feedback mechanisms, such as complaint processes, helpdesk statistics, and other user feedback (e.g., surveys, interviews, or focus groups);
(c) Threat analysis, threat reporting, and threat intelligence feeds that are available;
(d) Fraud trends, fraud investigation results, and fraud metrics as available; and
(e) The results of ongoing customer experience assessments and privacy assessments.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The purpose of control EI-1 is to fully understand the performance of their identity system, organizations will need to identify critical inputs to their continuous evaluation process.

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs SHALL document their metrics, reporting requirements, and data inputs for any CSP, IdP, or other integrated identity service to ensure that expectations are appropriately communicated to partners and vendors.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the RP has documented their metrics, reporting requirements, and data inputs for any CSP, IdP, or other integrated identity service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documents for the continuous evaluation and improvement process to ensure they include the RPs metrics, reporting requirements, and data inputs for any CSP, IdP, or other integrated identity service.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The documentation of metrics, reporting requirements, and data inputs for any CSP, IdP, or other integrated identity service is to ensure that expectations are appropriately communicated to partners and vendors.

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs and CSPs SHALL enable individuals to convey grievances and seek redress through an issue handling process that is documented, accessible, trackable, and usable by all individuals and whose instructions are easy to find on a public-facing website.

part.name: objective
part.p: (1) Determine if the RPs and CSPs issues handline process is:
(a) Documented,
(b) Accessible,
(c) Trackable,
(e) Usable by all individuals, and has instructions on an easy-to-find, public-facing website.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test the issues handling process public-facing website to ensure the instructions are easy to find and follow, and the issues are documented, accessible, trackable, and usable (i.e., 508 compliant).

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs and CSPs SHALL institute a governance model for implementing this issue handling process, including documented roles and responsibilities.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the RPs and CSPs instituted a governance model for implementing the issue handling process that includes documented roles and responsibilities.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the issuance handling governance model documentation to ensure it includes documented roles and responsibilities.

control.title: Redress - Issue Handling Function - Evidence Review

part.name: statement
part.p: The issue handling process SHALL be implemented as a dedicated function that includes procedures for impartially reviewing pertinent evidence.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the issue handling process is implemented as a dedicated function with procedures for impartially reviewing pertinent evidence.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the issuance handling documentation for descriptions of how it is implemented to ensure it is implemented as a dedicated function that includes procedures for impartially reviewing pertinent evidence.

control.title: Redress - Issue Handling Function - Additional Evidence

part.name: statement
part.p: The issue handling process SHALL be implemented as a dedicated function that includes procedures for requesting and collecting additional evidence that informs the issues.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the issue handling process is implemented as a dedicated function with procedures for requesting and collecting additional evidence that informs the issues.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the issuance handling documentation for descriptions of how it is implemented to ensure it is implemented as a dedicated function that includes procedures for requesting and collecting additional evidence that informs the issues.

part.name: statement
part.p: The issue handling process SHALL be implemented as a dedicated function that includes procedures for expeditiously resolving issues and determining corrective action.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the issue handling process is implemented as a dedicated function with procedures for expeditiously resolving issues and determining corrective action.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the issuance handling documentation for descriptions of how it is implemented to ensure it is implemented as a dedicated function that includes procedures for expeditiously resolving issues and determining corrective action.

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs and CSPs SHALL make human support personnel available to intervene and override issue adjudication outputs generated by algorithmic support mechanisms.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if RPs and CSPs have made human support personnel available to intervene and override issue adjudication outputs generated by algorithmic support mechanisms.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the human support personnel whose role is to intervene and override issue adjudication outputs generated by algorithmic support mechanisms to ensure they are available.

control.title: Redress - Support Personnel Education - Issue Handling

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs and CSPs SHALL educate support personnel on issue handling procedures for the digital identity management system.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if RPs and CSPs have educated support personnel on issue handling procedures for the digital identity management system.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the support personnel to ensure they are educated on issue handling procedures for the digital identity management system.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the training materials used to train the support personnel in issue handling procedures for the digital identity management system.

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs and CSPs SHALL educate support personnel on the avenues for redress.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if RPs and CSPs have educated support personnel on the avenues for redress.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the support personnel to ensure they are educated on the avenues for redress.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the training materials used to train the support personnel on the avenues for redress.

control.title: Redress - Support Personnel Education - Access Alternatives

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs and CSPs SHALL educate support personnel on the alternatives available to gain access to services.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if RPs and CSPs have educated support personnel on the alternatives available to gain access to services.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview the support personnel to ensure they are educated on the alternatives available to gain access to services.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the training materials used to train the support personnel on the alternatives available to gain access to services.

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs and CSPs SHALL implement a process for personnel and technologies that provides support functions to report and address major barriers that end users face and grievances they may have.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the RP/CSP has implemented a process for personnel and technologies that provides support functions to report and address major barriers that end users face and grievances they may have.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the issues handling process documentation to ensure it includes processes for personnel and technologies that support functions to report and address major barriers that end users face and grievances they may have.

part.name: statement
part.p: RPs and CSPs SHALL incorporate findings derived from the issue handling process into continuous evaluation and improvement activities.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the RP/CSP has incorporated findings derived from the issue handling process into continuous evaluation and improvement activities.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the evaluation inputs for the continuous evaluation and improvement program to ensure they incorporate findings derived from the issue handline process.

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL assess the integrity and performance of their redress mechanisms.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the integrity and performance of their redress mechanisms are being assessed.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the issues handling process documentation for policies and practices that describe how to assess the integrity and performance of their redress mechanisms.

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL implement controls to prevent, detect, and remediate attempted identity fraud involving those mechanisms.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if controls to prevent, detect, and remediate attempted identity fraud involving the redress mechanisms have been implemented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the issues handling process documentation for policies and practices that describe the controls they implement to prevent, detect, and remediate attempted identity fraud involving those mechanisms.

control.title: Cybersecurity, Fraud, and Identity Program Integrity - Information Exchange

part.name: statement
part.p: Organizations SHALL establish consistent mechanisms for the exchange of information between stakeholders that are responsible for critical internal security and fraud prevention.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if consistent mechanisms for the exchange of information between stakeholders that are responsible for critical internal security and fraud prevention have been established.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine mechanisms used for the exchange of information between stakeholders that are responsible for critical internal security and fraud prevention.

control.title: Cybersecurity, Fraud, and Identity Program Integrity - Privacy Assessment

part.name: statement
part.p: All data collected, transmitted, or shared by the identity service provider SHALL be subject to a detailed privacy and legal assessment by either the entity generating the data (e.g., a CSP) or the related RP for whom the service is provided.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if all data collected, transmitted, or shared by the identity service provider is subject to a detailed privacy and legal assessment.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine privacy and legal assessments to ensure one exists for all data collected, transmitted, or shared by the identity service provider,

part.name: guidance
part.p: The privacy and legal assessment can be done by either the entity generating the data (e.g., a CSP) or the related RP for whom the service is provided.

control.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Identity Systems - Documentation

prop.name: marking
prop.value: AI, ML, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning

part.name: statement
part.p: All uses of AI/ML [in the identity system] SHALL be documented.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if all uses of AI/ML in the identity system have been documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation describing all uses of AI/ML.

control.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Identity Systems - Communication

prop.name: marking
prop.value: AI, ML, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning

part.name: statement
part.p: All uses of AI/ML [in the identity system] SHALL be communicated to organizations that rely on these systems.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if all uses of AI/ML in the identity system have been communicated to organizations that rely on these systems.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine communications to ensure all uses of AI/ML in the identity system have been communicated to organizations that rely on them.

control.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Identity Systems - Disclosure to RPs

prop.name: marking
prop.value: AI, ML, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning

part.name: statement
part.p: The use of integrated technologies that leverage AI/ML by CSPs, IdPs, or verifiers SHALL be disclosed to all RPs that make access decisions based on information from these systems.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the use of integrated technologies that leverage AI/ML is disclosed to all RPs that make access decisions based on information from these systems.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine communications from CSP/IdPs to RPs that make access decisions based on information from systems to ensure disclosure of any use of integrated technologies that leverage AI/ML.

control.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Identity Systems - AI/ML Model Information - Training Methods

prop.name: marking
prop.value: AI, ML, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning

part.name: statement
part.p: All organizations that use AI/ML SHALL provide information to any entities that use their technology [including] the methods and techniques used for training their models.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if methods and techniques used for training AI/ML models have been provided to the entities using the AI/ML technology.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine AI/ML documentation that is shared with entities that use their technology to ensure it includes the methods and techniques used for training their AI/ML models.

control.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Identity Systems - AI/ML Model Information - Training Data Sets

prop.name: marking
prop.value: AI, ML, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning

part.name: statement
part.p: All organizations that use AI/ML SHALL provide information to any entities that use their technology [including] a description of the data sets used in training.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if a description of the data sets used in training the AI/ML models have been provided to the entities using the AI/ML technology.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine AI/ML documentation that is shared with entities that use their technology to ensure it includes a description of the data sets used in training.

control.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Identity Systems - AI/ML Model Information - Updates

prop.name: marking
prop.value: AI, ML, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning

part.name: statement
part.p: All organizations that use AI/ML SHALL provide information to any entities that use their technology [including] the frequency of model updates.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the frequency of AI/ML model updates have been provided to the entities using the AI/ML technology.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine AI/ML documentation that is shared with entities that use their technology to ensure it includes the frequency of model updates.

control.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Identity Systems - AI/ML Model Information - Algorithm Testing

prop.name: marking
prop.value: AI, ML, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning

part.name: statement
part.p: All organizations that use AI/ML SHALL provide information to any entities that use their technology [including] the results of all testing completed on their algorithms.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine if the results of all testing completed on their AI/ML algorithms have been provided to the entities using the AI/ML technology.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine AI/ML documentation that is shared with entities that use their technology to ensure it includes the results of all testing completed on their algorithms.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs SHALL evaluate the risks associated with each identity proofing option offered (e.g., identity proofing types, validation sources, assistance mechanisms) and implement mitigating fraud controls, as appropriate.

part.name: objective
part.p: Confirm that the CSP has assessed the risks associated with each identity proofing option offered and that they have employed appropriate mitigations to address those risks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the CSP's risk assessment results and confirm it has assessed the risks associated with each identity proofing option offered and has implemented mitigating fraud controls, as appropriate.

part.name: guidance
part.p: CSPs are likely to provide different options for how applicants can complete the identity proofing process. This control ensures a risk assessment process is in place to evaluate these options and identify and address unique risks. It can be done as part of the DIRM process defined in NIST SP 800-63-4 or an organizational specific risk management process.

part.name: statement
part.p: At a minimum, CSPs SHALL design each option such that the options provide comparable assurance in aggregate.

part.name: objective
part.p: Confirm that the CSP has designed its identity services so that no identity proofing pathway (sequence of actions) results in a lower level of assurance than another.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the CSP's documentation to confirm that the risk assessment identifies the risks unique to each identity proofing option and that the risks have been mitigated sufficiently to provide comparable assurance.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs SHALL identify which roles are applicable to their identity service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Confirm that the CSP has identified the roles that are employed as part of its identity proofing service.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the CSP's practices statement or other documentation to determine the roles it employs in its identity service.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Identity proofing roles are proofing agent, trusted referee, applicant reference, and process assistant.

part.name: statement
