part.p: The verifier SHALL comply with its respective records retention policies in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and policies, including any National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) records retention schedules that may apply.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine compliance with records retention policy requirements.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the CSP's records retention policy and evaluate its applicability with laws and regulations. Where applicable, audit a sample of retained records to ensure that their retention is consistent with policy.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the verifier opts to retain records in the absence of mandatory requirements, the verifier or the CSP or IdP of which it is a part SHALL conduct a risk management process [NISTRMF], including assessments of privacy and security risks, to determine how long records should be retained and SHALL inform the subscriber of that retention policy.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify justification for records retention not covered by mandatory requirements.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine evidence to determine risk-based decision for records retention was used, and that notice to subscribers is provided.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Non-mandatory records retention.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL employ appropriately tailored privacy controls defined in [SP800-53] or an equivalent industry standard.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine compliance with relevant overall privacy requirements.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the CSP's operating procedure documentation and, as applicable, authority-to-operate (ATO) for consistency with SP 800-53 or equivalent standard.

part.name: statement
part.p: If CSPs or IdPs process attributes for purposes other than identity services (i.e., identity proofing, authentication, or attribute assertions), related fraud mitigation, or compliance with laws or legal processes, they SHALL implement measures to maintain predictability and manageability commensurate with the privacy risks that arise from the additional processing.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine compliance with relevant privacy requirements for supplemental services.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the CSP's documented policies or practices to determine which predictability and manageability measures it employs, (e.g., notice, consent, selective disclosure).

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when there is non-identity use of identity attributes.

part.name: statement
part.p: When CSPs or IdPs use consent measures, they SHALL NOT make consent for the additional processing a condition of the identity service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that consent measures are voluntary.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine terms of use to ensure that additional consent is not a requirement.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when consent is requested from subscriber.

part.name: statement
part.p: The agency SHALL consult with their Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP) and conduct an analysis to determine whether the collection of personal information to issue or maintain authenticators triggers the requirements of the Privacy Act of 1974 [Privacy Act] (see Sec. 7.4).

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine when Privacy Act requirements are triggered.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation to determine that consultation with the SAOP occurred and that all determinations of whether the service is subject to the privacy act of 1974 have been recorded.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview to confirm that the agency has consulted with its SAOP to determine if the service is subject to the Privacy Act of 1974.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to federal agencies and others acting on their behalf.

part.name: statement
part.p: The agency SHALL publish a System of Records Notice (SORN) to cover such collections, as applicable.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that a SORN is published when required.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the agency's System of Records Notice, as applicable.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to federal agencies only.

part.name: statement
part.p: The agency SHALL consult with its SAOP and conduct an analysis to determine whether the collection of personal information to issue or maintain authenticators triggers the requirements of the E-Government Act of 2002 [E-Gov].

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine when E-Government Act requirements are triggered.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview to confirm that the agency offering or using the identity proofing service has consulted with its SAOP to determine if the service is subject to the E-Government Act of 2002.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation of the SAOP assessment.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to federal agencies only.

part.name: statement
part.p: The agency SHALL publish a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to cover such collection, as applicable.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that a PIA is published when required.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the agency's Privacy Impact Assessment, as applicable.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to federal agencies and others providing services to federal agencies.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier and associated CSP or IdP SHALL provide mechanisms for the redress of subscriber complaints and problems that arise from subscriber authentication processes, as described in Sec. 5.6 of [SP800-63].

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that useful redress for authentication problems is provided.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test redress mechanisms from the viewpoint of the claimant.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine redress mechanisms from the viewpoint of the claimant.

part.name: statement
part.p: These mechanisms SHALL be easy for subscribers to find and use.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that redress mechanisms are usable by the population of subscribers.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test redress mechanisms to determine their ease of use.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP or IdP SHALL assess the mechanisms for efficacy in resolving complaints or problems.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that redress mechanisms are sufficient to resolve expected authentication problems.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP or IdP operator to determine the results of their assessment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Passwords SHALL either be chosen by the subscriber or assigned randomly by the CSP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Establish acceptable methods of password creation (e.g., no default passwords).

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by creating a new account or changing a password to determine how password is chosen. If the password is not chosen by the subscriber.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP to establish that the password is assigned randomly.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the CSP disallows a chosen password because it is on a blocklist of commonly used, expected, or compromised values (see Sec. 3.1.1.2), the subscriber SHALL be required to choose a different password.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prohibit use of passwords expected to be commonly chosen.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to set an account to use a memorized secret that is on the blocklist. The attempt should fail.

part.name: statement
part.p: Other composition requirements for passwords SHALL NOT be imposed.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prohibit composition rules (e.g., requirement for specific character types).

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to create an unusual password that does not meet usual composition requirements (e.g., all lower case letters) and determine that it is accepted.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require passwords that are used as a single-factor authentication mechanism to be a minimum of 15 characters in length. Verifiers and CSPs MAY allow passwords that are only used as part of multi-factor authentication processes to be shorter but SHALL require them to be a minimum of eight characters in length.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require passwords to be long enough to provide baseline security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by trying to create a password that does not meet the minimum length requirements and verify that it is not accepted.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers and CSPs SHOULD accept Unicode [ISO/IEC 10646] characters in passwords. Each Unicode code point SHALL be counted as a single character when evaluating password length.

part.name: objective
part.p: Allow use of characters memorable to the subscriber, even if they use a language not represented by ASCII.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by creating a password containing a Unicode character such as an accented vowel and determine that it is accepted, and that the unaccented version of the same character does not allow successful authentication.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT impose other composition rules (e.g., requiring mixtures of different character types) for passwords.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prohibit composition rules (e.g., requirement for specific character types)

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: See PASSAUTH-3

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT require subscribers to change passwords periodically. However, verifiers SHALL force a change if there is evidence that the authenticator has been compromised.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prohibit password rotation, which has been shown to cause selection of weaker passwords.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview to determine from CSP that periodic password changes are not required, but that a mechanism is in place to force password changes for affected subscribers after a breach.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT permit the subscriber to store a hint (e.g., a reminder of how the password was created) that is accessible to an unauthenticated claimant.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prohibit use of password hints, which greatly weaken security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to ensure that there is no provision for a password hint to be displayed to unauthenticated claimants and that there is no provision for storing a hint in subscribers' account management.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT prompt subscribers to use knowledge-based authentication (KBA) (e.g., "What was the name of your first pet?") or security questions when choosing passwords.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prohibit use of KBA, which greatly weakens security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to ensure that there is no authentication flow that involves the use of KBA and that there is no provision for storing authentication questions and answers in subscribers' account management.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL request the password to be provided in full (not a subset of it) and SHALL verify the entire submitted password (e.g., not truncate it).

part.name: objective
part.p: Require use of the entire password for authentication to maximize the security benefit of the whole password.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine verification code to ensure that entire password is verified.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by creating long passwords and attempting to authenticate with truncated passwords.

part.name: statement
part.p: When processing a request to establish or change a password, verifiers SHALL compare the prospective secret against a blocklist that contains known commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require use of a blocklist to prevent selection of excessively weak passwords.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP to determine contents of the blocklist.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to ensure that it is not possible to change a password to a blocklist entry.

part.name: statement
part.p: The entire password SHALL be subject to comparison, not substrings or words that might be contained therein.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the entire password is verified so that the full security benefit of long passwords is realized.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to ensure that a long password containing a blocklist entry is accepted.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the chosen password is found on the blocklist, the CSP SHALL require the subscriber to select a different secret and SHALL provide the reason for rejection.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require selection of a different password if a weak one is chosen.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to ensure that a substitute for a blocklisted password is requested.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL offer guidance to the subscriber to help the subscriber choose a strong password. This is particularly important following the rejection of a password on the blocklist as it discourages trivial modifications of listed weak passwords [Blocklists].

part.name: objective
part.p: Require coaching of the subscriber on selection of better passwords if a weak one is initially chosen.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to determine that helpful advice on choosing strong passwords is offered.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 3.2.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Strengthen verifier against online password guessing attacks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making a large number of incorrect authentication attempts and ensure that number and/or rate of attempts is limited.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL allow the use of password managers and autofill functionality.

part.name: objective
part.p: Allow subscriber to use a password manager, which aids in the use of strong and unguessable passwords.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to authenticate using one or more popular password managers and verify that a password stored in the manager can be filled in.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL use approved encryption and an authenticated protected channel when requesting passwords.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the communication channel to the verifier is secure against eavesdropping.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test password transmission to verify that an authenticated protected channel such as TLS is used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine encryption algorithms used to verify that they are approved.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL store passwords in a form that is resistant to offline attacks.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require strong storage to protect against offline attacks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Requirement is satisfied by PV-16 through PV-18.

part.name: statement
part.p: Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable password hashing scheme.

part.name: objective
part.p: At a minimum, require salting and hashing of passwords as protection against offline attacks should the verifier be breached.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine password verification storage to determine evidence of password hashing and salt storage.

part.name: statement
part.p: The salt SHALL be at least 32 bits in length and chosen to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes (i.e., to prevent multiple subscriber accounts from having the same hashed password).

part.name: objective
part.p: Require use of a salt sufficient to ensure that two subscribers with the same password do not hash to the same value in the verifier.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine stored salt values to ensure that they are at least 32 bits in length.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP personnel to determine that salt is chosen to avoid collisions.

part.name: statement
part.p: Both the salt value and the resulting hash SHALL be stored for each password.

part.name: objective
part.p: Describes the use of a salt.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Requirement is satisfied by verification method of PV-16.

part.name: statement
part.p: If used, this key value SHALL be generated by an approved random bit generator, as described in Sec. 3.2.1.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: For keyed hashing, require appropriate selection of the key.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP personnel to determine how the key value is generated.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when keyed hashing is used.

part.name: statement
part.p: The secret key value SHALL be stored separately from the hashed passwords.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require separate storage for a keyed hash key so it is not also breached if the hashed passwords are.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP personnel to determine how the key value is stored.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when keyed hashing is used.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs that create look-up secret authenticators SHALL use an approved random bit generator, as described in Sec. 3.2.12, to generate the list of secrets.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require selection of sufficiently random look-up secrets

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code used to generate look-up secrets.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs that create look-up secret authenticators SHALL deliver the authenticator list securely to the subscriber (e.g., in an in-person session, via an online session, through the postal mail to a contact address).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that eavesdroppers and other intermediaries do not have access to look-up secrets being delivered to the subscriber.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP to determine the possible methods for delivering look-up secrets to subscribers.

part.name: statement
part.p: If delivered via an online session, the session SHALL be authenticated by the subscriber at AAL2 or higher and SHALL deliver the secrets through an authenticated protected channel and in accordance with the post-enrollment binding requirements in Sec. 4.1.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that online delivery of look-up secrets is sufficiently secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by requesting delivery of look-up secrets online, and ensure that a minimum of AAL2 authentication is required and that an authenticated protected channel such as TLS is used.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when look-up secrets are delivered online.

part.name: statement
part.p: Look-up secrets SHALL be at least six decimal digits (or equivalent) in length. Additional requirements described in Sec. 3.1.2.2 may also apply, depending on their length.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that look-up secrets are sufficiently long to provide adequate security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine look-up secrets received in response to a request and verify that they are at least six decimal digits or equivalent in length.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers of look-up secrets SHALL prompt the claimant for a secret from their authenticator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify appropriate authentication flow.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by authenticating with a look-up secret authenticator and verify the prompt.

part.name: statement
part.p: A secret from a look-up secret authenticator SHALL be used successfully only once.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that look-up secrets are replay resistant.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to authenticate using the same look-up secret more than once and verify that subsequent attempts are unsuccessful.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL store look-up secrets in a form that is resistant to offline attacks.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require strong storage to protect against offline attacks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Requirement is satisfied by LSV-4 and LSV-6 through LSV-8.

part.name: statement
part.p: All lookup secrets SHALL be stored in a hashed form using an approved hashing function.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require use of a hashing function known to be sufficiently secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine hashing function used.

part.name: statement
part.p: Look-up secrets SHALL be at least six decimal digits (or equivalent) in length, as specified in Sec. 3.1.2.1.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that look-up secrets are sufficiently long to provide adequate security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: See LSA-3.

part.name: statement
part.p: Look-up secrets that are shorter than the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication) SHALL be stored in a salted and hashed form using a suitable password hashing scheme, as described in Sec. 3.1.1.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require salting for look-up secrets that are at risk of collision with other secrets.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine look-up secret verification storage to determine evidence of password hashing and salt storage.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to look-up secrets shorter than 112 bits.

part.name: statement
part.p: The salt value SHALL be at least 32 bits in length and arbitrarily chosen to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require use of a salt sufficient to ensure that two subscribers with the same look-up secrets do not hash to the same value in the verifier.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine stored salt values to ensure that they are at least 32 bits in length.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP personnel to determine that salt is chosen to avoid collisions.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to look-up secrets shorter than 112 bits.

part.name: statement
part.p: Both the salt value and the resulting hash SHALL be stored for each lookup secret.

part.name: objective
part.p: Describes the use of a salt.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Requirement is satisfied by verification method of LSV-6.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to look-up secrets shorter than 112 bits.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 3.2.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Strengthen verifier against online look-up secret guessing attacks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making a large number of incorrect authentication attempts and ensure that number and/or rate of attempts is limited.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL use approved encryption and an authenticated protected channel when requesting look-up secrets.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that online delivery of look-up secrets is sufficiently secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Requirement is satisfied by LSA-2.

part.name: statement
part.p: The out-of-band authenticator SHALL establish a separate channel with the verifier to retrieve the out-of-band secret or authentication request.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that a separate channel is used to communicate with the verifier.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to verify that the secondary channel is established with a separate device or that it is established with an independent application on the authenticating device.

part.name: statement
part.p: Communication over the secondary channel SHALL use approved encryption unless sent via the public switched telephone network (PSTN).

part.name: objective
part.p: Establish that delivery of the out-of-band secret is delivered securely.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by requesting an out-of-band secret and verify that an authenticated protected channel such as TLS is used or that is it delivered via the PSTN.

part.name: statement
part.p: Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication because it may be vulnerable to:
(a) Access using only a password.
(b) Interception in transit or at intermediate mail servers.
(c) Rerouting attacks, such as those caused by Domain Name System (DNS) spoofing.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prohibit the use of email for delivery of out-of-band secrets because of multiple security vulnerabilities.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to authenticate and verify that there is no option to use email for out-of-band authentication.

part.name: statement
part.p: The out-of-band authenticator SHALL uniquely authenticate itself in one of the following ways when communicating with the verifier:

(a) Using approved cryptography, establish a mutually authenticated protected channel (e.g., client-authenticated transport layer security (TLS) [RFC8446]) with the verifier. Communication between the out-of-band authenticator and the verifier MAY use a trusted intermediary service to which each authenticates. The key used to establish the channel SHALL be provisioned in a mutually authenticated session during authenticator binding, as described in Sec. 4.1.

(b) Authenticate to a public mobile telephone network using a SIM card or equivalent secret that uniquely identifies the subscriber. This method SHALL only be used if a secret is sent from the verifier to the out-of-band device via the PSTN (i.e., SMS or voice) or an encrypted instant messaging service; use a wired connection to the PSTN that the verifier can call and dictate the out-of-band secret. For the purposes of this definition, "wired connection" includes services such as cable providers that offer PSTN services through other wired media and fiber via analog telephone adapters.

part.name: objective
part.p: Confirm that out-of-band secrets are delivered only to authenticated devices.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to verify that one of the specified methods is used to authenticate the device receiving an out-of-band secret.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the out-of-band authenticator requests approval over the secondary communication channel rather than by presenting a secret that the claimant transfers to the primary communication channel, it SHALL accept a transfer of the secret from the primary channel and send it to the verifier over the secondary channel to associate the approval with the authentication transaction.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that authentication approval over the secondary channel requires transfer of a secret from the primary channel to avoid approval fatigue attacks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test, if present, secondary channel approval to verify that it requires entry of a secret obtained from the primary channel.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL NOT store the identifying key itself but SHALL use a verification method (e.g., an approved hash function or proof of possession of the identifying key) to uniquely identify the authenticator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that, should the verifier be compromised, any active out-of-band secrets are protected from disclosure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine verifier storage of out-of-band secrets to verify that they are protected from compromise.

part.name: statement
part.p: Depending on the type of out-of-band authenticator, one of the following SHALL take place:

(a) Transfer of the secret from the secondary to the primary channel. As shown in Fig. 1, the verifier MAY signal the device that contains the subscriber's authenticator to indicate a readiness to authenticate. It SHALL then transmit a random secret to the out-of-band authenticator and wait for the secret to be returned via the primary communication channel.

(b) Transfer of the secret from the primary to the secondary channel. As shown in Fig. 2, the verifier SHALL transmit a random authentication secret to the claimant via the primary channel. It SHALL then wait for the secret to be returned via the secondary channel from the claimant's out-of-band authenticator. The verifier MAY additionally display an address, such as a phone number or VoIP address, for the claimant to use in addressing its response to the verifier.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that one of the approved authentication flows involving the transfer of a secret from one device or application to another is used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test out-of-band authentication to verify that one of the given authentication flows is used.

part.name: statement
part.p: In all cases, the authentication SHALL be considered invalid unless completed within 10 minutes.

part.name: objective
part.p: Make sure that out-of-band secrets are only valid for the short term.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test out-of-band authentication by delaying slightly more than 10 minutes before transferring the secret and verify that authentication is unsuccessful.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL accept a given authentication secret as valid only once during the validity period to provide replay resistance, as described in Sec. 3.2.7.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that out-of-band secrets are replay resistant.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to authenticate and ensure that a given out-of-band secret can be used only once.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL generate random authentication secrets that are at least six decimal digits (or equivalent) in length.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that out-of-band secrets are sufficiently long to provide adequate security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine look-up secrets received in response to a request and verify that they are at least six decimal digits or equivalent in length.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL generate random authentication secrets using an approved random bit generator as described in Sec. 3.2.12.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require selection of sufficiently random look-up secrets.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code used to generate look-up secrets.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the authentication secret is less than 64 bits long, the verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the total number of consecutive failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account as described in Sec. 3.2.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that out-of-band authentication is sufficiently protected against online guessing attacks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making a large number of incorrect authentication attempts and ensure that number and/or rate of attempts is limited.

part.name: statement
part.p: Generating a new authentication secret SHALL NOT reset the failed authentication count.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that obtaining a new out-of-band secret does not bypass the rate limiting mechanism.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making a large number of incorrect authentication attempts and ensure that number and/or rate of attempts is limited even if a new authentication secret is obtained.

part.name: statement
part.p: Use of the PSTN for out-of-band verification is restricted as described in this section and SHALL satisfy the requirements of Sec. 3.2.9.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke restricted authenticator provisions.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by RESTA-1 and RESTA-2.

part.name: statement
part.p: Setting or changing the pre-registered telephone number is considered to be the binding of a new authenticator and SHALL only occur as described in Sec. 4.1.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Defend against attackers who attempt to change the pre-registered telephone number.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by changing pre-registered telephone number and verify that requirements BAA-2 and BAA-3 are satisfied.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL ensure that alternative authenticator types are available to all subscribers and SHOULD remind subscribers of this limitation of PSTN out-of-band authenticators before binding one or more devices controlled by the subscriber.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that subscribers understand the risks associated with PSTN out-of-band authentication.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by RESTA-2.

part.name: statement
part.p: Each use of the authenticator SHALL require the presentation of the activation factor.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that a previously activated authenticator cannot be coopted by an attacker.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by authenticating more than once with the same authenticator and verify that the activation factor is required each time. Also satisfied by MFOBA-4.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticator activation secrets SHALL meet the requirements of Sec. 3.2.10.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke requirements for activation secrets.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by AS-1 through AS-8.

part.name: statement
part.p: A biometric activation factor SHALL meet the requirements of Sec. 3.2.3, including limits on the number of consecutive authentication failures.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke requirements for biometric authentication factors.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by UB-1 through UB-4.

part.name: statement
part.p: The password or biometric sample used for activation and any biometric data derived from the biometric sample (e.g., a fingerprint image and feature locations produced by a fingerprint feature extractor) SHALL be erased immediately after an authentication operation.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the activation factor cannot be used or extracted following an authentication operation.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to establish that activation factor is erased as required.

part.name: statement
part.p: The secret key and its algorithm SHALL provide at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the key used to generate the OTP is of sufficient size to be secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine the security strength of the key used to generate the OTP.

part.name: statement
part.p: The nonce SHALL be of sufficient length to ensure that it is unique for each operation of the authenticator over its lifetime.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the nonce is large enough that the OTP sequence doesn't repeat.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine if the nonce is sufficiently long to not repeat during the expected lifetime of the authenticator.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the nonce used to generate the authenticator output is based on a real-time clock, the nonce SHALL be changed at least once every two minutes.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the nonce of a time-based OTP changes frequently enough.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to determine that the OTP changes at least once every two minutes.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to time-based OTP authenticators.

part.name: statement
part.p: The symmetric keys used by authenticators are also present in the verifier and SHALL be strongly protected against unauthorized disclosure by access controls that limit access to the keys to only those software components that require access.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against attacks on verifier.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of OTP generation keys to determine whether they are strongly protected.

part.name: statement
part.p: When binding a single-factor OTP authenticator to a subscriber account, the verifier or associated CSP SHALL use approved cryptography for key establishment to generate and exchange keys or to obtain the secrets required to duplicate the authenticator output.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that only secure, well-vetted cryptographic algorithms are being used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code or documentation showing the algorithms being used and verify that they are NIST approved.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL use approved encryption and an authenticated protected channel when collecting the OTP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that only secure, well-vetted cryptographic algorithms and protocols are being used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documented policies or code to determine that only approved cryptographic algorithms can be used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine secure use of a protocol such as TLS for communication with the claimant.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL accept a given OTP only once while it is valid to provide replay resistance, as described in Sec. 3.2.7.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that OTP use is replay resistant.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to ensure that it is not possible to successfully use the same OTP value for two different authentication transactions while it is valid.

part.name: statement
part.p: Time-based OTPs [TOTP] SHALL have a defined lifetime that is determined by the expected clock drift in either direction of the authenticator over its lifetime plus an allowance for network delay and claimant entry of the OTP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that OTP will not fail prematurely due to clock drift.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine specifications for authenticator clock drift and planned lifetime and ensure that time tolerance of OTP entry is sufficiently long.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to time-based OTP authenticators.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHOULD implement or, if the authenticator output is less than 64 bits in length, SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 3.2.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against OTP guessing attacks

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making a large number of incorrect authentication attempts and ensure that number and/or rate of attempts is limited.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when authenticator output if less than 64 bits in length.

part.name: statement
part.p: Each use of the authenticator SHALL require the input of the activation factor.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that all use of the authenticator is protected by the activation factor.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to authenticate and verify that the activation factor is needed for each authentication.

part.name: statement
part.p: The secret key and its algorithm SHALL provide at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the key used to generate the OTP is of sufficient size to be secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine the security strength of the key used to generate the OTP.

part.name: statement
part.p: The nonce SHALL be of sufficient length to ensure that it is unique for each operation of the authenticator over its lifetime.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the nonce is large enough that the OTP sequence doesn't repeat.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine if the nonce is sufficiently long to not repeat during the expected lifetime of the authenticator.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the nonce used to generate the authenticator output is based on a real-time clock, the nonce SHALL be changed at least once every two minutes.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the nonce of a time-based OTP changes frequently enough.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to determine that the OTP changes at least once every two minutes.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to time-based OTP authenticators.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticator activation secrets SHALL meet the requirements of Sec. 3.2.10.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke requirements for activation secrets.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by AS-1 through AS-8.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Authenticator uses activation secrets.

part.name: statement
part.p: A biometric activation factor SHALL meet the requirements of Sec. 3.2.3, including limits on the number of consecutive authentication failures.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke requirements for biometric authentication factors.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by UB-1 through UB-4.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Authenticator uses biometric activation.

part.name: statement
part.p: The unencrypted key and activation secret or biometric sample and any biometric data derived from the biometric sample (e.g., a fingerprint image and feature locations produced by a fingerprint feature extractor) SHALL be erased immediately after an OTP has been generated.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the activation factor cannot be used or extracted following an authentication operation.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to establish that activation factor is erased as required.

part.name: statement
part.p: The symmetric keys used by authenticators SHALL be strongly protected against unauthorized disclosure by access controls that limit access to the keys to only those software components that require access.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against attacks on verifier.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of OTP generation keys to determine whether they are strongly protected.

part.name: statement
part.p: When binding a multi-factor OTP authenticator to a subscriber account, the verifier or associated CSP SHALL use approved cryptography for key establishment to generate and exchange keys or to obtain the secrets required to duplicate the authenticator output.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that only secure, well-vetted cryptographic algorithms are being used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code or documentation showing the algorithms being used and verify that they are NIST approved.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL use approved encryption and an authenticated protected channel when collecting the OTP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that only secure, well-vetted cryptographic algorithms and protocols are being used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documented policies or code to determine that only approved cryptographic algorithms can be used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine secure use of a protocol such as TLS for communication with the claimant.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL accept a given OTP only once while it is valid to provide replay resistance, as described in Sec. 3.2.7.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that OTP use is replay resistant.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to ensure that it is not possible to successfully use the same OTP value for two different authentication transactions while it is valid.

part.name: statement
part.p: Time-based OTPs [TOTP] SHALL have a defined lifetime that is determined by the expected clock drift in either direction of the authenticator over its lifetime plus an allowance for network delay and claimant entry of the OTP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that OTP will not fail prematurely due to clock drift.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine specifications for authenticator clock drift and planned lifetime and ensure that time tolerance of OTP entry is sufficiently long.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of consecutive failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as required by Sec. 3.2.10.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against OTP guessing attacks

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making a large number of incorrect authentication attempts and ensure that number and/or rate of attempts is limited.

part.name: statement
part.p: Single-factor cryptographic authenticators used at AAL3 SHALL use public-key cryptography to protect the authentication secrets from compromise of the verifier.

part.name: objective
part.p: Avoid the use of shared authentication secrets that could be compromised by an attacker.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation of verifiers to determine that they only store public keys for cryptographic authenticators

part.name: statement
part.p: If they are accessible to the endpoint being authenticated, exportable authentication keys SHALL be strongly protected against unauthorized disclosure with access controls that limit access to the key to only those software components that require access.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against attacks on authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of authentication keys to determine whether they are strongly protected.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to exportable authentication keys.

part.name: statement
part.p: Nonexportable authentication keys (usable at AAL3 or below) SHALL be stored in an isolated execution environment that is protected by hardware or in a separate processor with a controlled interface to the central processing unit of the user endpoint.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against attacks on authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of authentication keys to determine whether they are stored in an isolated execution environment.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to non-exportable authentication keys.

part.name: statement
part.p: External (i.e., non-embedded) cryptographic authenticators SHALL meet the requirements for connected authenticators in Sec. 3.2.11.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure integrity of endpoint-authenticator connection.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by CONNAUTH-1 through CONNAUTH-3, and if wireless, WC-1 through WC-7.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to non-embedded cryptographic authenticators.

part.name: statement
part.p: While both types of keys SHALL be protected against modification, symmetric keys SHALL additionally be protected against unauthorized disclosure by access controls that limit access to the key to only those software components that require access.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against attacks on verifier.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of authentication keys to determine whether they are strongly protected.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when symmetric authentication keys are used.

part.name: statement
part.p: The authentication key and its algorithm SHALL provide at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the authentication key is of sufficient size to be secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine the security strength of the authentication key.

part.name: statement
part.p: The challenge nonce SHALL be at least 64 bits in length and SHALL either be unique over the authenticator's lifetime or statistically unique (i.e., generated using an approved random bit generator, as described in Sec. 3.2.12).

part.name: objective
part.p: Provide strong protection against replay attacks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code used to generate the authentication nonce.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verification operation SHALL use approved cryptography.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that only secure, well-vetted cryptographic algorithms and protocols are being used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documented policies or code to determine that only approved cryptographic algorithms can be used.

part.name: statement
part.p: Multi-factor cryptographic authenticators used at AAL3 SHALL use public-key cryptography to protect the authentication secrets from compromise of the verifier.

part.name: objective
part.p: Avoid the use of shared authentication secrets that could be compromised by an attacker.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation of verifiers to determine that they only store public keys for cryptographic authenticators.

part.name: statement
part.p: Multi-factor cryptographic authenticators encapsulate one or more authentication keys that SHALL only be accessible through the presentation and verification of an activation factor (i.e., a password or a biometric characteristic).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that authenticator enforces use of an activation factor.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of authentication secret to determine that the secret is only accessible upon presentation of a valid activation factor.

part.name: statement
part.p: Non-exportable authentication keys, suitable for use at AAL3, SHALL be stored in an isolated execution environment that is protected by hardware or in a separate processor with a controlled interface to the central processing unit of the user endpoint.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against attacks on authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of authentication keys to determine whether they are stored in an isolated execution environment.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to non-exportable authentication keys.

part.name: statement
part.p: If accessible to the endpoint being authenticated, authentication keys SHALL be strongly protected against unauthorized disclosure by using access controls that limit access to the authentication keys to only those software components that require access.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against attacks on authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of authentication keys to determine whether they are strongly protected.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to exportable authentication keys.

part.name: statement
part.p: External (non-embedded) cryptographic authenticators SHALL meet the requirements for connected authenticators in Sec. 3.2.11.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure integrity of endpoint-authenticator connection.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by CONNAUTH-1 through CONNAUTH-3, and if wireless, WC-1 through WC-7.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to non-embedded cryptographic authenticators.

part.name: statement
part.p: Each authentication event SHALL require input and verification of the local activation factor.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that a previously activated authenticator cannot be coopted by an attacker.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by authenticating more than once with the same authenticator and verify that the activation factor is required each time.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticator activation secrets SHALL meet the requirements of Sec. 3.2.10.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke requirements for activation secrets.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by AS-1 through AS-8.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Authenticator uses activation secrets.

part.name: statement
part.p: A biometric activation factor SHALL meet the requirements of Sec. 3.2.3, including limits on the number of consecutive authentication failures.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke requirements for biometric authentication factors.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by UB-1 through UB-4.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Authenticator uses biometric activation.

part.name: statement
part.p: The activation secret or biometric sample and any biometric data derived from the biometric sample (e.g., a fingerprint image and feature locations produced by a fingerprint feature extractor) SHALL be erased after an authentication transaction.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the activation factor cannot be used or extracted following an authentication operation.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to establish that activation factor is erased as required.

part.name: statement
part.p: Requirements for a multi-factor cryptographic verifier are identical to those for a single-factor cryptographic verifier.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure baseline requirements for cryptographic verifiers are met.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by SFCVER-1 through SFCVER-4

part.name: statement
part.p: If a flag indicating use of an activation factor is present and indicates that an activation factor was not used, the authentication SHALL be treated as single-factor.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that an activation factor was used if indication was provided.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine if the activation factor flag is checked and heeded, if provided.

part.name: statement
part.p: Access to the private key SHALL require an activation factor.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that authenticator enforces use of an activation factor.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of authentication secret to determine that the secret is only accessible upon presentation of a valid activation factor.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticator activation secrets SHALL meet the requirements of Sec. 3.2.10.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke requirements for activation secrets.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by AS-1 through AS-8.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Authenticator uses activation secrets.

part.name: statement
part.p: Biometric activation factors SHALL meet the requirements of Sec. 3.2.3, including limits on the number of consecutive authentication failures.

part.name: objective
part.p: Invoke requirements for biometric authentication factors.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by UB-1 through UB-4.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Authenticator uses biometric activation.

part.name: statement
part.p: The password or biometric sample used for activation and any biometric data derived from the biometric sample SHALL be erased immediately after an authentication transaction.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the activation factor cannot be used or extracted following an authentication operation.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to establish that activation factor is erased as required.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authentication processes using subscriber-controlled wallets SHALL be used with a federation process as detailed in Sec. 5 of [SP800-63C].

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that subscriber-controlled wallets are used in connection with federation requirements.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine federation process and verify compliance with requirements in Section 5 of SP 800-63C

part.name: statement
part.p: Assertions that lack a valid signature from the wallet or an audience restriction SHALL NOT be considered phishing-resistant.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that wallets satisfy applications requiring phishing resistance.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine assertions or code generating them to determine if valid signatures or audience restrictions are present.

part.name: statement
part.p: Assertions SHALL also include sufficient information to determine the nature of the activation method used to activate the wallet.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that activation information is provided to relying parties.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine assertions or code generating them to determine if the activation method is included.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs SHALL provide subscriber instructions for appropriately protecting the authenticator against theft or loss.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that subscribers understand their responsibilities for protecting authenticators.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by establishing a new subscriber account and observe whether sufficient instructions are provided.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL provide a mechanism to invalidate the authenticator immediately upon notification from a subscriber that the authenticator's loss, theft, or compromise is suspected.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that subscribers have a meaningful way to report authenticator issues and that appropriate action is taken.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by simulating the loss of an authenticator and determine whether instructions are provided to the subscriber to handle this situation and that appropriate action is taken when reported.

part.name: statement
part.p: When required by the authenticator type descriptions in Sec. 3.1, the verifier SHALL implement controls to protect against online guessing attacks.

part.name: objective
part.p: Control online guessing attacks.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by RL-2 through RL-6

part.name: statement
part.p: Unless otherwise specified in the description of a given authenticator, the verifier SHALL limit consecutive failed authentication attempts using a specific authenticator on a single subscriber account to no more than 100 by disabling that authenticator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Set overall upper limit on consecutive failed authentication attempts.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making 101 authentication failures with an authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine subscriber account to verify that the authenticator has been disabled.

part.name: statement
part.p: If more than one authenticator is involved with an excessive number of authentication attempts (e.g., single-factor cryptographic authenticator and centrally verified password), both authenticators SHALL be disabled.

part.name: objective
part.p: Address excessive authentication failures involving more than one authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making excessive authentication failures with two authenticators.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine subscriber account to verify that both authenticators have been disabled.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticators that have been disabled SHALL be required to rebind to the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 4.1, to be usable in the future.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that disabled authenticators are treated as unbound to the subscriber account.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by causing an authenticator to be disabled due to excessive authentication failures and verify that there is no way to successfully use the authenticator other than to go through the authenticator binding procedure.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the retry count of an authenticator is reset following a successful authentication, the maximum AAL of the authenticator being reset SHALL not exceed the AAL of the session from which it is being reset.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prevent AAL escalation due to authenticator retry count reset.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by authenticating unsuccessfully and then successfully with a given authenticator and examine the maximum AAL at which it can be used to verify that it does not increase.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to verifiers that reset the unsuccessful authentication count after successful authentication.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the subscriber cannot authenticate at the required AAL, the account recovery procedures in Sec. 4.2 SHALL be used.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require account recovery in the event that authenticator rebinding is unavailable.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by section 4.2 compliance

part.name: statement
part.p: Biometrics SHALL only be used as part of multi-factor authentication with a physical authenticator (i.e., "something you have").

part.name: objective
part.p: Block use of biometric comparison as a single factor or with only a password.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test available authentication methods to ensure that all require a physical authenticator.

part.name: statement
part.p: The biometric characteristic SHALL be presented and compared for each authentication operation.

part.name: objective
part.p: Do not allow biometric characteristics to be cached.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making multiple authentications using biometric comparison and verify that the biometric characteristic is required to be presented each time.

part.name: statement
part.p: An alternative nonbiometric authentication option SHALL always be provided to the subscriber.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require alternatives in the event that a biometric characteristic cannot be presented for some reason.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test available authentication methods to ensure that an alternative to biometric comparison is always available.

part.name: statement
part.p: Biometric data SHALL be treated and secured as sensitive personal information.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that biometric data is sufficiently protected.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of biometric data and evaluate access controls for that data.

part.name: statement
part.p: The biometric system SHALL operate with an FMR [ISO/IEC2382-37] of one in 10000 or better for all demographic groups.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure biometric comparison is sufficiently secure against false matches.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine test results or certifications for biometric system

part.name: statement
part.p: Demographic categories to be considered SHALL include sex and skin tone when these factors affect biometric performance.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure biometric comparison works for a wide demographic range.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine test procedure for biometric system to verify that a wide demographic range was included.

part.name: statement
part.p: This FMR SHALL be achieved under the conditions of a conformant attack (i.e., zero-effort impostor attempt), as defined in [ISO/IEC30107-1].

part.name: objective
part.p: Define test conditions for false match rate test.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine test procedure to determine test conditions.

part.name: statement
part.p: Biometric performance SHALL be tested in accordance with [ISO/IEC19795-1].

part.name: objective
part.p: Define test conditions for false match rate test.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine test procedure to determine test conditions.

part.name: statement
part.p: The biometric system SHALL be configured with a fixed threshold; it is not feasible to change the threshold for each demographic.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require consistent match criteria for all demographic groups.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine comparison algorithm to verify that it uses a single threshold.

part.name: statement
part.p: The biometric system SHOULD implement PAD for iris and fingerprint modalities and SHALL implement PAD for facial recognition.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require PAD for facial recognition to counter deepfakes.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test facial recognition with a synthetic image to verify use of presentation attack detection.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to facial recognition modality.

part.name: statement
part.p: Biometric comparison based on voice SHALL NOT be used.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prohibit use of voice recognition due to ease in spoofing.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test available authentication methods to verify that voice recognition is not available.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to voice recognition modality.

part.name: statement
part.p: The biometric system SHALL allow no more than five consecutive failed authentication attempts or 10 consecutive failed attempts if PAD is implemented and meets the above requirements.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit opportunity to spoof biometric comparison.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by creating unsuccessful comparisons and verify that requests are throttled after the specified limit is reached.

part.name: statement
part.p: Once that limit has been reached, the biometric authenticator SHALL impose a delay of at least 30 seconds before each subsequent attempt with an overall limit of no more than 50 consecutive failed authentication attempts or 100 if PAD is implemented due to the mitigation of presentation attacks.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit opportunity to spoof biometric comparison.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by creating unsuccessful comparisons and verify that requests are throttled after the specified limit is reached.

part.name: statement
part.p: Once the overall limit is reached, the biometric system SHALL disable biometric authentication and offer another factor (e.g., a different biometric modality or an activation secret if it is not a required factor) if such an alternative method is already available.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit opportunity to spoof biometric comparison.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by creating unsuccessful comparisons and verify that biometric comparison is disabled when the specified limit is reached.

part.name: statement
part.p: The presentation of a biometric factor for authenticator activation SHALL be a separate operation from unlocking the host device (e.g., smartphone).

part.name: objective
part.p: Minimize opportunity for an attacker to authenticate on an already unlocked device.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to authenticate on an already unlocked device and verify that an additional biometric comparison is required.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the comparison is performed centrally, the sender or endpoint SHALL be authenticated before capturing the biometric sample from the claimant.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against injection attacks from rogue hardware devices.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine method for authenticating sensor or endpoint and evaluate its security

part.name: guidance
part.p: Central biometric comparison.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the comparison is performed centrally, appropriate controls (e.g., encryption and access controls) for sensitive personal information SHALL be implemented.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that centrally stored biometric data is sufficiently secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of biometric data and evaluate access controls for that data.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Central biometric comparison.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the comparison is performed centrally, an authenticated protected channel between the sensor (or an endpoint containing a sensor that resists sensor replacement) and the verifier SHALL be established. All transmission of biometric information SHALL be conducted over that authenticated protected channel.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that biometric data is transmitted securely for central comparison.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code or communications protocol to verify that all biometric data is transmitted over an authenticated protected channel.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Central biometric comparison.

part.name: statement
part.p: The biometric samples and any other biometric data derived from them SHALL be erased immediately after any adaptation or research data has been derived.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that biometric samples are securely erased as soon as they are no longer needed.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to verify erasure of biometric samples.

part.name: statement
part.p: A limit on the allowable time for adaptation SHALL be established and enforced by the authenticator or the CSP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Establish reasonable limits on adaptation time to limit persistence of biometric samples.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation to determine adaptation time limit.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to verify that biometric samples are erased at or before that time limit.

part.name: statement
part.p: Attestations SHALL be signed using a digital signature that provides at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the key used to sign the attestation is of sufficient size to be secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine the security strength of the attestation key.

part.name: statement
part.p: Approved cryptographic algorithms SHALL be used to establish phishing resistance where required.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that only secure, well-vetted cryptographic algorithms and protocols are being used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documented policies or code to determine that only approved cryptographic algorithms can be used.

part.name: statement
part.p: Keys used for phishing resistance SHALL provide at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the authentication key is of sufficient size to be secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine the security strength of the authentication key.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticators that involve the manual entry of an authenticator output (e.g., out-of-band and OTP authenticators) SHALL NOT be considered phishing-resistant because the manual entry does not bind the authenticator output to the specific session being authenticated.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that manual intervention, which can be socially engineered, is not part of phishing-resistant authentication.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test available authentication methods to ensure that phishing -resistant authentication methods do not use manual entry.

part.name: statement
part.p: An authentication protocol with channel binding SHALL establish an authenticated protected channel with the verifier.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that phishing-resistant authentication uses a secure channel that authenticates the verifier.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by to verify that authenticated protected channel such as TLS is used.

part.name: statement
part.p: The protocol SHALL then strongly and irreversibly bind a channel identifier negotiated in establishing the authenticated protected channel to the authenticator output (e.g., by signing the two values together using a private key controlled by the claimant for which the public key is known to the verifier).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the authentication protocol is bound to the communications channel.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to determine if client-authenticated TLS is being used or analyze protocol to verify channel binding.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verifier SHALL validate the signature or other information used to prove phishing resistance.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that authentication requires a valid signature.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to verify that invalid signatures are not accepted.

part.name: statement
part.p: An authentication protocol with verifier name binding SHALL establish an authenticated protected channel with the verifier.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that phishing-resistant authentication uses a secure channel that authenticates the verifier.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by to verify that authenticated protected channel such as TLS is used.

part.name: statement
part.p: The protocol SHALL generate an authenticator output that is cryptographically bound to a verifier identifier that is authenticated as part of the protocol.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the authentication transaction can only succeed when connected to a specific host or domain.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by simulating connection to a different host or domain and verify that the transaction does not succeed.

part.name: statement
part.p: In the case of DNS identifiers, the verifier identifier SHALL be either the authenticated hostname of the verifier or a parent domain that is at least one level below the public suffix [PSL] associated with that hostname.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure the correct relationship between the transaction hostname and the bound verifier name.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine code to determine that the correct comparison is made between the bound host/domain and the hostname of the authenticated protected channel.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the verifier and CSP or IdP are separate entities (as shown by the dotted line in Fig. 3 of [SP800-63]), communications between the verifier and CSP or IdP SHALL occur through a mutually authenticated protected channel (e.g., a client-authenticated TLS connection) using approved cryptography.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure a secure relationship between verifier and CSP/IdP.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine communications channel between verifier and CSP/IdP and verify that client-authenticated TLS or equivalent is used.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when verifier and CSP/IdP are separate entities.

part.name: statement
part.p: The authenticator itself SHALL establish authentication intent.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that authentication only occurs when intended by the claimant.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test available authentication methods to ensure that all require some action on the part of the claimant.

part.name: statement
part.p: In scenarios involving biometric authentication not requiring claimant action, an explicit mechanism (e.g., tapping a software or physical button) SHALL be provided to establish authentication intent.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that "passive" biometric authentication is not sufficient to establish intent.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test available authentication methods using biometrics to ensure that all require some action on the part of the claimant.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to authentication methods using biometric comparison.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the RP determines that the risk to any party is unacceptable, the restricted authenticator SHALL NOT be used, and an alternative authenticator type SHALL be used.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that restricted authenticators are not used in high-risk situations.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine risk assessment for evaluation and acceptability of risks.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL offer subscribers at least one alternative authenticator that is not restricted and can be used to authenticate at the required AAL.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that alternative authentication methods not using restricted authenticators are provided.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine available authentication methods to verify that one or more non-restricted authenticators can be used.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL provide subscribers with meaningful notice regarding the restricted authenticator's security risks and the availability of unrestricted alternatives.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that subscribers are aware of the risks and alternatives.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine text displayed to subscriber when binding a restricted authenticator to make sure meaningful notice is displayed.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL address any additional risks to subscribers and RPs in its risk assessment.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that risks are documented.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine risk assessment for documentation of any additional risks.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL develop a migration plan for the possibility that the restricted authenticator will not be acceptable in the future and include this migration plan in its Digital Identity Acceptance Statement (see Sec. 3.4.4 of [SP800-63]).

part.name: objective
part.p: Plan for the likelihood that restricted authenticators will be non-compliant in the future.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine migration plan to verify a plan for deprecation/removal of restricted authenticator.

part.name: statement
part.p: In all cases, the activation secret SHALL remain within the authenticator and its associated user endpoint.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that activation secret remains secure.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine protocol between authenticator or endpoint and verifier and confirm that activation secret is not transmitted.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticators that use activation secrets SHALL require the secrets to be at least four characters in length and SHOULD require the secrets to be at least six characters in length.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that activation secret is not too easy to guess.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to establish an activation secret that is three characters or less and verify that it is not accepted.

part.name: statement
part.p: The authenticator or verifier SHALL implement a retry-limiting mechanism that limits the number of consecutive failed activation attempts using the authenticator to no more than 10.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the verification process limits excessive retries that would indicate a brute force attack.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by making more than 10 consecutive incorrect activation secret entries followed by a successful one and verify that authentication does not succeed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Unless the authenticator generates an invalid output when an incorrect activation secret is provided, retry limiting SHALL be implemented in the authenticator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that it is not possible to do an offline activation attack by observing the authenticator output.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to activate the authenticator offline and ensure that it is locally throttled.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Does not apply when the authenticator provides an output, but a wrong one, when an activation secret is provided.

part.name: statement
