part.p: Once the limit of attempts is reached, the authenticator SHALL be disabled, and a different authenticator SHALL be required for authentication.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that an authenticator that has reached its limit of activation attempts cannot be easily reactivated.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine procedures for use of an authenticator that has reached its activation attempts limit and verify that rebinding of the authenticator to the subscriber account is required.

part.name: statement
part.p: For authenticators that are usable at AAL3, verification of activation secrets SHALL be performed in a hardware-protected environment (e.g., a secure element, TPM, or TEE).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that authenticator protects activation secrets sufficiently for use at AAL3.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation of authenticator to verify that activation secret verification is hardware-protected.

part.name: statement
part.p: At AAL2, if a hardware-protected environment is not used, the authenticator SHALL use the activation secret to derive a key used to decrypt the authentication key.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the authentication key is protected by knowledge of the activation secret.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine storage of the authentication key and verify it is the result of a decrypting the stored key with a key derived from the activation secret.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when authentication key is stored in a software protected environment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Submitting the activation factor SHALL be a separate operation from unlocking the host device (e.g., smartphone).

part.name: objective
part.p: Minimize opportunity for an attacker to authenticate on an already unlocked device.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to authenticate on an already unlocked device and verify that a separate entry of the activation secret is required.

part.name: statement
part.p: This connection SHALL be made using a wired connection (e.g., USB or direct connection with a smartcard), a wireless technology, or a hybrid of those technologies, including network connections.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that connection to the authenticator meets an accepted model.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine ways that a connected authenticator can be used and verify that it meets one of the three models for connection.

part.name: statement
part.p: Approved cryptography SHALL be used for all cases in which cryptographic operations are required.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that only secure, well-vetted cryptographic algorithms and protocols are being used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documented policies or code to determine that only approved cryptographic algorithms can be used.

part.name: statement
part.p: All communication of authentication data between authenticators and endpoints SHALL occur directly between those devices or through an authenticated protected channel between the authenticator and endpoint.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require secure communications between authenticator and endpoint.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine protocol for any communications between authenticator and endpoint that may be indirect (through intermediaries).

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when communication between authenticator and endpoint is not point-to-point.

part.name: statement
part.p: To minimize the attack surface for threats to the authenticator-endpoint connection, the authentication process SHALL require physical proximity between the authenticator and endpoint by establishing a wireless connection with a range of no more than 240 meters.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit opportunity for attack by remotely located attackers.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test authentication process with a remotely located authenticator and verify that it fails.

part.name: statement
part.p: Wireless connections SHALL establish a key for encrypted communication between the authenticator and endpoint in one of the following ways:
(1) Through a temporary wired connection between the devices.

(2) Through an association process that is similar to a pairing process but does not require a persistent relationship between devices to establish a key for encrypted communication between the authenticator and endpoint.

part.name: objective
part.p: Define acceptable methods for associating authenticator and endpoint.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test key establishment between endpoint and authenticator and verify that it is done in an acceptable way.

part.name: statement
part.p: If an association process is used, it SHALL employ a pairing code or other shared secret between the devices.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require use of a shared secret to identify the parties to the association.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test association process and verify that a pairing code or shared secret is required.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when an association process is used instead of a temporary wired connection.

part.name: statement
part.p: If an association process is used, either the authenticator or endpoint SHALL have a pairing code that is at least six decimal digits (or equivalent) in length that MAY be printed on the device.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require that the pairing code be long enough to provide appropriate security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test association process and verify that the pairing code or shared secret is long enough.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when an association process is used instead of a temporary wired connection.

part.name: statement
part.p: If an association process is used, the pairing code SHALL be conveyed between the devices by manual entry or using a QR code or similar representation that is optically communicated.

part.name: objective
part.p: Allow use of manual or optically-assisted entry of pairing code.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test association process to verify that the pairing code is manually entered or optically communicated.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when an association process is used instead of a temporary wired connection.

part.name: statement
part.p: When using a wireless technology with an effective range of less than 1 meter (e.g., NFC), any activation secret transmitted from the endpoint to the authenticator SHALL be encrypted using a key that is established between the devices.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure secure transmission of the activation secret from the endpoint to the authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that transmission of the activation secret is encrypted using a key established between the devices.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when very short range (<1 m) wireless technologies are used.

part.name: statement
part.p: A pairing code SHALL be used if the authenticator is configured to require authenticated pairing.

part.name: objective
part.p: Use pairing processes appropriate for the authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to verify that a pairing code is used when authenticated pairing is required.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when authenticator uses authenticated pairing.

control.title: Wireless Authenticator Non-Proximate Authenticated Protected Channel

part.name: statement
part.p: Network connections and wireless technologies with an effective range of 1 meter or more (e.g., Bluetooth Low Energy [BLE]) SHALL use an authenticated protected channel between the authenticator and endpoint.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require stronger protections for wireless connections with longer range.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that an authenticated protected channel such as TLS is used.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when longer range (>=1 m) wireless technologies are used.

part.name: statement
part.p: The entire authentication transaction SHALL be encrypted.

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect authentication transaction in transit between devices.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that the entire transaction is authenticated.

part.name: statement
part.p: A mechanism for endpoints to remove persistent keys SHALL be provided.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require removal of associations between authenticator and endpoint when no longer needed.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test authenticator and/or endpoint to verify that a mechanism to remove persistent keys exists.

part.name: statement
part.p: Hybrid connections (e.g., hybrid transports specified by the CTAP2.2 protocol) SHALL be established between authenticators and endpoints in one of the following ways:

(1) By communicating initial keying information and the identity of the tunnel service to be used via a displayed QR code or similar visual representation coupled with the receipt by the endpoint of wireless data containing the additional information required to establish the tunnel connection.
(2) Through cached keying and tunnel information retained by the authenticator and endpoint from a previous authentication transaction.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require hybrid connections to be established securely or to be based on cached information.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test establishment of hybrid connections between authenticators and endpoints to verify that they are established in one of the permitted methods.

part.name: statement
part.p: The wireless data SHALL be conveyed over a technology with a maximum effective range of no more than 240 meters.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit opportunity for attack by remotely located attackers.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test authentication process with a remotely located authenticator and verify that it fails.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when initial keying information is being established.

part.name: statement
part.p: A mechanism for endpoints to remove cached associations with authenticators SHALL be provided.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require removal of associations between authenticator and endpoint when no longer needed.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test authenticator and/or endpoint to verify that a mechanism to remove persistent keys exists.

part.name: statement
part.p: Unless otherwise specified, random values that reference this section SHALL be generated by an approved random bit generator that provides at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of SP800-131A (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication).

part.name: objective
part.p: Require use of sufficiently secure random values.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation of random bit generator to verify that it meets SP 800-131A requirements.

part.name: statement
part.p: To be considered non-exportable, an authenticator SHALL either be a separate piece of hardware or an embedded processor or execution environment (e.g., secure element, TEE, TPM).

part.name: objective
part.p: Require that non-exportable keys not be directly accessible to the endpoint.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation, including APIs, to ensure that authentication keys are not sent or accessible outside the authenticator.

part.name: statement
part.p: A non-exportable authenticator SHALL be designed to prohibit the export of the authentication secret to the host processor and SHALL NOT be capable of being reprogrammed by the host processor to allow the secret to be extracted.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that reprogramming of the secure environment is not possible as a back door to obtain access to authentication secrets.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine APIs between the endpoint and authenticator to verify that it is not possible for the endpoint to reprogram the authenticator.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticators SHALL be bound to subscriber accounts by either: being issued by the CSP as part of enrollment; or using a subscriber-provided authenticator that is acceptable to the CSP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Allow CSP to verify that all authenticators bound to subscriber accounts meet their requirements.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine procedures for binding authenticators and verify that they provide an opportunity for the CSP to verify the authenticator's security.

part.name: statement
part.p: Throughout the lifetime of a digital identity, CSPs SHALL maintain a record of all authenticators that are bound to each subscriber account.

part.name: objective
part.p: Maintain the ability to audit authenticators that are or have been bound to subscriber accounts.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine CSP records to verify that records of current and past bound authenticators are maintained.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL determine the characteristics of the authenticator being bound (e.g., single-factor versus multifactor, phishing-resistant or not) so that verifiers can assess compliance with the requirements at each AAL.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that authenticators bound to subscriber accounts meet requirements for the AALs at which they will be used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Interview CSP to determine the sufficiency of procedures for approving authenticators.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL also maintain other state information that is required to meet the authenticator verification requirements.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the CSP is equipped to maintain other state information such as that required for throttling.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine CSP records to verify that required state information is maintained.

part.name: statement
part.p: The record created by the CSP SHALL contain the date and time of significant authenticator life cycle events (e.g., binding to the subscriber account, renewal, update, expiration).

part.name: objective
part.p: Maintain the ability to audit authenticator life cycle events.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine CSP records to verify that authenticator life cycle events are documented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Accordingly, CSPs SHALL permit the binding of multiple authenticators to a subscriber account.

part.name: objective
part.p: Allow subscribers to bind multiple authenticators to guard against loss or failure of a given authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to bind multiple authenticators and verify that it is successful.

part.name: statement
part.p: When any new authenticator is bound to a subscriber account, the CSP SHALL ensure that the process requires authentication at either the maximum AAL currently available in the subscriber account or the maximum AAL at which the new authenticator will be used, whichever is lower.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that it is not possible to increase authenticated AAL by binding a new authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by binding a new authenticator for use at AAL2 or AAL3 and verify that it requires authentication at the corresponding AAL.

part.name: statement
part.p: When an authenticator is added, the CSP SHALL notify the subscriber via a mechanism independent of the transaction binding the new authenticator, as described in Sec. 4.6.

part.name: objective
part.p: Warn subscriber in case an authenticator is bound without their knowledge.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by binding an additional authenticator and verify that the subscriber receives a notification as described.

part.name: statement
part.p: The binding process SHALL proceed in one of the following ways:
(1) An endpoint that has authenticated to the CSP requests a binding code from the CSP. The binding code is input into the endpoint associated with the new authenticator and sent to the CSP.
(2) The endpoint associated with the new authenticator obtains a binding code from the CSP. The binding code is input to an authenticated endpoint and sent to the CSP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the binding of authenticators not directly connected to an authenticated session uses a secure process.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by binding an authenticator that is not connected to the authenticated endpoint, and ensure that it uses one of the described processes.

part.name: statement
part.p: When binding an external authenticator, an authenticated protected channel SHALL be established by the endpoint associated with the new authenticator and the CSP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that channel between authenticator and endpoint are protected against eavesdropping and intermediaries.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that an authenticated protected channel such as TLS is used.

part.name: statement
part.p: When binding an external authenticator, the CSP SHALL generate a binding code using an approved random bit generator as described in Sec. 3.2.12 and send it to either the new authenticator endpoint or the authenticated endpoint approving the binding.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that a sufficiently random binding code is used and transmitted to the endpoint or authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to see how the binding code is generated.

control.title: External Authenticator Identifier Binding Code Length

part.name: statement
part.p: The binding code SHALL be at least 40 bits in length if it is used with an identifier entered by the subscriber on the new authenticator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the binding code is sufficiently large to provide the required level of security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by binding an external authenticator and verify that the binding code is sufficiently long.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when an identifier is entered by the subscriber on the new authenticator.

control.title: External Authenticator Non-Identifier Binding Code Length

part.name: statement
part.p: The binding code SHALL be at least 112 bits in length if it is not used with an identifier entered by the subscriber on the new authenticator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the binding code is sufficiently large to provide the required level of security.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by binding an external authenticator and verify that the binding code is sufficiently long.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when no identifier is entered by the subscriber on the new authenticator.

part.name: statement
part.p: When binding an external authenticator, the subscriber SHALL transfer the binding code to the other endpoint manually or via a local out-of-band method such as a QR code.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the binding code is transferred through action by the subscriber.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test all supported methods for binding an external authenticator and verify that manual or local out-of-band action is required.

part.name: statement
part.p: The binding code SHALL NOT be communicated over an insecure channel.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that the binding code is not available to an attacker.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test all supported methods for binding an external authenticator and verify that no insecure channels are used.

part.name: statement
part.p: When binding an external authenticator, the binding code SHALL be usable only once.

part.name: objective
part.p: Guard against replay of the binding code.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to use the same binding code more than once and verify that it fails.

part.name: statement
part.p: The binding code SHALL be valid for a maximum of 10 minutes.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit usability of a binding code that may have been part of an incomplete binding transaction.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to bind an external authenticator while delaying transfer of the binding code for more than 10 minutes, and verify that it fails.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL provide clear instructions on what the subscriber should do in the event of an authenticator binding mishap.

part.name: objective
part.p: Provide recourse for binding transactions that do not occur normally.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting to bind an external authenticator and verify that suitable guidance to the subscriber is provided.

part.name: statement
part.p: The binding of subscriber-provided authenticators SHALL be done as described in Sec. 4.1.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that subscriber-provided authenticators are bound in a secure manner.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine procedures for binding subscriber-controlled authenticators and verify that they meet BAA-1 through BAA-3 and BINAE-1 through BINAE-9 as applicable.

part.name: statement
part.p: The types of authenticators accepted by the CSP SHALL be documented in the CSP practice statement.

part.name: objective
part.p: Make sure clear guidelines for subscriber acceptability are published.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine CSP practice statement to verify that acceptable types of subscriber-provided authenticators are documented.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs SHALL support one or more of the four account recovery mechanisms described.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that secure account recovery mechanisms are provided.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine available recovery procedures to verify that at least one of the described account recovery mechanisms is supported.

part.name: statement
part.p: The use of alternative methods SHALL be based on a risk analysis and documented by the CSP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require that alternative recovery mechanisms by documented and accompanied by a valid risk analysis.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine risk analysis for any alternative account recovery mechanisms that are supported.

part.name: statement
part.p: The recovery code SHALL include at least 64 bits from an approved random bit generator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that a sufficiently random recovery code is used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to see how the recovery code is generated.

part.name: statement
part.p: The issuance of a replacement recovery code SHALL result in an account recovery notification, as described in Sec. 4.6.

part.name: objective
part.p: Confirm that subscriber is notified of account recovery events.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by performing a recovery using a saved recovery code and verify that the subscriber is notified in one of the ways described.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verification of saved recovery codes SHALL be subject to the throttling requirements in Sec. 3.2.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit ability to guess recovery codes.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by performing a recovery using a number of invalid recovery codes followed by a correct code and confirm that throttling has occurred.

part.name: statement
part.p: Saved recovery codes SHALL be stored in the subscriber account in hashed form using an approved one-way function, as described in Sec. 3.1.1.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: At a minimum, require salting and hashing of recovery codes as protection against offline attacks should the verifier be breached.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine recovery code verification storage to determine evidence of hashing.

part.name: statement
part.p: Following the use of a saved recovery code, the CSP SHALL invalidate that recovery code and SHALL issue a new saved recovery code to the subscriber.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prevent replay of recovery codes.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by attempting a second recovery using a saved recovery code and verify that it is unsuccessful.

part.name: statement
part.p: The issued recovery code SHALL include at least six decimal digits (or equivalent) from an approved random bit generator, as described in Sec. 3.2.12.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that a sufficiently random recovery code is used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to see how the recovery code is generated.

part.name: statement
part.p: Issued recovery codes SHALL be valid for at most:
(a) 21 days when sent to a postal address within the contiguous United States.
(b) 30 days when sent to a postal address outside of the contiguous United States.
(c) 10 minutes when sent via text message or voice.
(d) 24 hours when sent to an email address.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit lifetimes of issued recovery codes based on expected delivery times.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine methods for issued recovery code delivery and verify that implementation limits their validity to within the specified timeframes.

part.name: statement
part.p: The verification of issued recovery codes SHALL be subject to the throttling requirements in Sec. 3.2.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Limit ability to guess recovery codes.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by performing a recovery using a number of invalid recovery codes followed by a correct code and confirm that throttling has occurred.

part.name: statement
part.p: When establishing recovery addresses other than those validated or verified as part of the identity proofing process, the address SHALL be verified.

part.name: objective
part.p: Confirm reliability of recovery addresses.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine metadata associated with recovery addresses and verify that a confirmation flag is present and is required in order to be used for recovery.

control.title: Issued Recovery Code Address Verification Procedure

part.name: statement
part.p: To verify an address, the CSP SHALL send a confirmation code with the same characteristics as a recovery code to the newly established recovery address and require that the subscriber return the same confirmation code to the CSP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Specify procedure for address confirmation.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by establishing a new recovery address and verify that it is only usable for recovery after having been confirmed.

control.title: Issued Recovery Code Multiple Address Requirement

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs SHALL allow the subscriber to establish at least two recovery addresses.

part.name: objective
part.p: Provide backup in case subscriber loses control of a recovery address.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by verifying that it is possible to establish more than one recovery address.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs that support the use of recovery contacts SHALL allow the subscriber to specify one or more addresses of trusted associates to receive issued recovery codes.

part.name: objective
part.p: Define recovery contacts mechanism.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by establishing a recovery contact and performing account recovery to verify that associate received recovery code and instructions on what to do with it.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the CSP supports the use of recovery contacts, the CSP SHALL provide methods for subscribers to view and manage recovery contacts.

part.name: objective
part.p: Allow subscriber to manage recovery contacts (e.g., to change them).

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by changing and deleting recovery contacts and verify that it is possible to do so.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL repeat the necessary steps of identity proofing consistent with the level of initial identity proofing and SHALL confirm that the claimant's identity is consistent with the previously established account.

part.name: objective
part.p: Define requirements for recovery via repeated identity proofing.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine procedures for recovery via identity proofing to verify their usability and security.

part.name: statement
part.p: The recovery of such subscriber accounts SHALL require the successful use of a saved recovery code, issued recovery code, or recovery contact.

part.name: objective
part.p: Define non-proofing recovery.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by ARM, IRC, and RECC controls

part.name: statement
part.p: To recover an account that can authenticate at a maximum of AAL2, the CSP SHALL require the subscriber to complete one of the following:
(1) Two recovery codes obtained using different methods from the set (i.e., saved, issued, and recovery contacts).
(2) One recovery code from the set (i.e., saved, issued, and recovery contacts) plus authentication with a single-factor authenticator that is bound to the subscriber account.
(3) Repeated identity proofing (provided that the subscriber account has been identity-proofed).

part.name: objective
part.p: Specify methods of account recovery at AAL2.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to verify that one recovery method is required to recover a single authentication factor, two methods are required to recover two authentication factors, or repeated identity proofing is required at AAL2.

part.name: statement
part.p: If an account that can authenticate at AAL3 has been identity-proofed at IAL3, the CSP SHALL successfully perform a successful biometric comparison against the biometric characteristic collected during an initial on-site attended identity proofing session, as described in [SP800-63A].

part.name: objective
part.p: Require biometric comparison for subscriber accounts to meet AAL3/IAL3 security requirements.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine procedures for account recovery at AAL3/IAL3 and verify that a successful biometric comparison is required.

part.name: statement
part.p: In all cases, account recovery SHALL cause a notification to be sent to the subscriber or their designee, as described in Sec. 4.6.

part.name: objective
part.p: Confirm that subscriber is notified of account recovery events.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by performing a recovery and verify that the subscriber is notified in one of the ways described.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL suspend, invalidate, or destroy compromised authenticators from the subscriber's account promptly following compromise detection.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require processes for rendering compromised authenticators inoperative.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine procedures for handling compromised authenticators and verify that such authenticators are disabled.

part.name: statement
part.p: Backup authenticators used for secure reporting of compromise SHALL be a password or a physical authenticator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Establish requirements for authenticators reporting compromise.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine procedures for issuing backup authenticators for reporting.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies if CSP issues an authenticator for reporting.

part.name: statement
part.p: When an authenticator expires, it SHALL NOT be usable for authentication.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that expired authenticators are not usable.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by trying to authenticate with an expired authenticator and verify that it is unsuccessful.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies if authenticators that expire are used.

part.name: statement
part.p: The replacement of expired authenticators SHALL conform to the binding process for an additional authenticator, as described in Sec. 4.1.2.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require standard issuance process for issuance of replacements for expired authenticators.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine CSP procedures for issuing replacements for expired authenticators and verify that the full issuance process is used.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies if authenticators that expire are used.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs SHALL promptly invalidate authenticators when a subscriber account ceases to exist (e.g., subscriber's death, the discovery of a fraudulent subscriber), when requested by the subscriber, when the authenticator is compromised, or when the CSP determines that the subscriber no longer meets its eligibility requirements.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require a process for invalidating authenticators when required.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine process for receiving and processing invalidation requests from subscriber and other appropriate sources.

part.name: statement
part.p: The CSP SHALL make a risk-based determination of the authenticity of invalidation requests from the subscriber.

part.name: objective
part.p: Guard against denial-of-service attacks from spurious invalidation requests.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine process for evaluating invalidation requests that are received.

part.name: statement
part.p: Events that require notification SHALL cause a notification to be sent to the notification addresses stored in the subscriber account. Notification addresses may be any means by which the subscriber can be reliably contacted, such as: postal address; email address; address (e.g., telephone number) to which a text message or voice message may be sent; and reference to the subscriber in a push notification service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Define overall requirement for notification.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that notification infrastructure exists.

part.name: statement
part.p: CSPs SHALL support at least two notification addresses per subscriber account.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require ability to establish multiple notification addresses for redundancy.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test establishment of multiple notification addresses and verify that it is possible to establish at least two.

part.name: statement
part.p: For subscriber accounts that have undergone identity proofing, at least one address SHALL have been validated during the identity proofing process.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require use of an identity proofed address for reliability.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test with an identity proofed subscriber account to verify that an identity proofed address is already used.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when subscriber account has been identity proofed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Notifications SHALL be sent to all notification addresses except postal addresses.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require transmission to multiple addresses except postal addresses due to cost considerations.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by generating a notification to a subscriber account with multiple non-postal notification addresses, and verify that the notification is sent to all of them.

part.name: statement
part.p: However, notifications SHALL be sent to postal addresses if no other form of notification address is stored in the subscriber account or if the notification is for account recovery at AAL3.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require notifications to postal addresses when they are the only notification address or for high assurance account recovery.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by generating a notification to subscriber accounts with only a postal address and by performing AAL3 account recovery and verify that a postal notification would be sent.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when the only notification address is a postal address or AAL3 recovery.

part.name: statement
part.p: Account recovery notifications SHALL also be sent to a postal address if the only other notification address in the subscriber account is the address to which an issued recovery code was sent.

part.name: objective
part.p: Provide postal notification when needed to provide notification independent of account recovery.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by using an issued recovery code and verify that a postal notification would be sent if no other notification address exists.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies when using issued recovery codes and the only other notification address is postal.

part.name: statement
part.p: The notification SHALL provide clear instructions, including contact information, in case the recipient repudiates the event associated with the notification.

part.name: objective
part.p: Provide recourse for account holders receiving notification of events they did not authorize.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine notification and verify presence of instructions and contact information.

part.name: statement
part.p: A session secret SHALL be shared between the subscriber's software and the accessed service.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require that a session establishment be based on a shared secret.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that a session secret is shared when a session is established based on authentication.

part.name: statement
part.p: The secret SHALL be directly presented by the subscriber's software, or possession of the secret SHALL be proven using a cryptographic mechanism.

part.name: objective
part.p: Allow verification of the secret to be either direct or cryptographic

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine process for verifying the shared secret to verify how it is verified.

part.name: statement
part.p: The continuity of authenticated sessions SHALL be based on the possession of a session secret that is issued by the session host at the time of authentication and optionally refreshed during the session. The nature of a session depends on the application, such as: a web browser session with a "session" cookie; and an instance of a mobile application that retains a session secret.

part.name: objective
part.p: Provide examples of session verification methods.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by SB-1 and SB-2.

part.name: statement
part.p: Cookies and similar "remember my browser" features SHALL NOT be used instead of authentication except as provided for reauthentication at AAL2 in Sec. 2.2.3 when the inactivity limit has been exceeded but the time limit has not.

part.name: objective
part.p: Emphasize that secrets may not be used to bypass multifactor authentication requirements.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that multifactor authentication requirements are enforced regardless of session secrets.

part.name: statement
part.p: However, RPs and CSPs SHALL ensure that the session lifetime limits described in Sec. 2.2.3 are enforced even when a knowledge of the session secret is demonstrated.

part.name: objective
part.p: Emphasize that secrets may not be used to bypass reauthentication time limits.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that reauthentication requirements are enforced regardless of session secrets.

part.name: statement
part.p: The secret used for session binding SHALL be generated by the session host in direct response to an authentication event.

part.name: objective
part.p: Specify party generating session secret.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine protocol to verify that session secret is generated by host upon authentication.

part.name: statement
part.p: A session MAY be considered at a lower AAL than the authentication event but SHALL NOT be considered at a higher AAL than the authentication event.

part.name: objective
part.p: Allow sessions to be used at lower AALs than authenticated.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to verify that it is possible to use a session at a lower AAL than was authenticated but not a higher AAL.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to relying parties that support applications at multiple AALs.

part.name: statement
part.p: Secrets used for session binding SHALL be established during or immediately following authentication.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require tight relationship between authentication and session binding.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by SB-6.

part.name: statement
part.p: Secrets used for session binding SHALL be established using input from an approved random bit generator, as described in Sec. 3.2.12, and are at least 64 bits in length.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that a sufficiently random session secret is used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to see how the session secret is generated and verify that it uses an approved random bit generator and is of sufficient length.

part.name: statement
part.p: Secrets used for session binding SHALL be erased or invalidated by the session subject when the subscriber logs out.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that sessions are no longer usable following logout.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that session secrets are no longer valid following logout.

part.name: statement
part.p: Secrets used for session binding SHALL be either transferred from the session host to the RP or CSP via an authenticated protected channel or derived from keys that are established as part of establishing a valid, mutually authenticated protected channel.

part.name: objective
part.p: Define secure methods of establishing the session secret.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that the session secret is transferred or derived as described.

part.name: statement
part.p: Secrets used for session binding SHALL time out and not be accepted after the times specified in Sec. 2.1.3, Sec. 2.2.3, and Sec. 2.3.3, as appropriate for the AAL.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that session secrets are invalidated when time out times are met.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that necessary timers are in place and used to invalidate session secrets.

part.name: statement
part.p: Secrets used for session binding SHALL be unavailable to intermediaries between the host and the subscriber's endpoint.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prevent intermediaries and eavesdroppers from accessing session secrets

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by SB-8.3.

part.name: statement
part.p: Following authentication, authenticated sessions SHALL NOT fall back to an insecure transport (e.g., from https to http).

part.name: objective
part.p: Prevent sessions from falling back to an insecure state

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test, if insecure transport is supported at all, by attempting to substitute an insecure transport and verify that it is unsuccessful.

part.name: statement
part.p: POST/PUT content SHALL contain a session identifier that the RP SHALL verify to protect against cross-site request forgery (CSRF).

part.name: objective
part.p: Protect against cross-site request forgery.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine content (e.g., with browser developer tools) to verify that session identifiers are present.

part.name: statement
part.p: The RP SHALL NOT interpret the presence of an access token as an indicator of the subscriber's presence in the absence of other signals.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that session secrets rather than access/refresh tokens define validity of a session.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by logging out of a federated session while a valid access token exists and verify that the session has been terminated.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to sessions established through federation. Note: last sentence of 5.1.2, "authentication session" -> "authenticated session"

part.name: statement
part.p: The periodic reauthentication of sessions SHALL be performed to confirm the subscriber's continued presence at an authenticated session (e.g., that the subscriber has not walked away without logging out).

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that a reauthentication process exists.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify use of a reauthentication process following session time out.

part.name: statement
part.p: When either the overall or inactivity timeout expires, the session SHALL be terminated.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that time out results in process termination.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by SB-8.4.

part.name: statement
part.p: Session activity SHALL reset the inactivity timeout, and successful reauthentication during a session SHALL reset both timeouts.

part.name: objective
part.p: Define criteria for resetting timeouts.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation of timeouts to verify that they are reset under these circumstances.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHALL establish and document the inactivity and overall time limits being enforced in a system security plan, such as that described in [SP800-39].

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify documentation of timeouts.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine system security plan to verify that timeouts are described.

part.name: statement
part.p: The IdP can communicate the time and details of the authentication event to the RP, but the RP SHALL be authoritative as to whether the reauthentication requirements have been met.

part.name: objective
part.p: Establish precedence for control of session timing.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation of timeouts at the RP to verify that it is not over-dependent on timing from the IdP.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to sessions established through federation.

part.name: statement
part.p: Collection, the storage of expected subscriber characteristics, and the processing of session characteristics SHALL be included in the privacy risk assessment described in Sec. 7.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify documentation of session monitoring.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine privacy risk assessment to verify that any use of session monitoring is included.

part.name: statement
part.p: Therefore, as stated in Sec. 2.4.3, when CSPs use consent measures, the subscriber's acceptance of additional uses SHALL NOT be a condition of providing authentication services.

part.name: objective
part.p: Ensure that consent measures are voluntary.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by PR-3.

part.name: statement
part.p: All keys SHALL be generated using approved cryptography.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that only secure, well-vetted cryptographic algorithms are being used.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documented policies or practices to determine that only approved cryptographic algorithms can be used.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authentication keys that are cloned or exported from a device to a sync fabric SHALL only be stored in an encrypted form using a key with the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication).

part.name: objective
part.p: Protection of authentication keys in the sync fabric.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine sync fabric implementation(s) to verify that keys are stored in encrypted form with sufficient strength.

part.name: statement
part.p: All authentication transactions SHALL perform private-key operations on the local device using cryptographic keys that are generated on-device or recovered from the sync fabric.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require cryptographic operations to be performed locally.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that the source of private keys is local or from the sync fabric.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authentication keys stored in the sync fabric SHALL be protected by access control mechanisms such that only the authenticated user can access their authentication keys in the sync fabric.

part.name: objective
part.p: Control access to keys in the sync fabric.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that authentication keys are only available to the subscriber.

part.name: statement
part.p: User access to authentication keys in the sync fabric SHALL be protected by AAL2-equivalent MFA to preserve the integrity of the authentication protocols using the synced keys.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require sufficient authentication to access keys in the sync fabric.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine sync fabric implementation(s) to verify that at least AAL2 authentication is required to access authentication keys.

part.name: statement
part.p: These general requirements and any other agency-specific requirements for using syncable authenticators SHALL be documented and communicated, including on public-facing websites and digital service policies, where applicable.

part.name: objective
part.p: Clearly document controls on use of syncable authenticators.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documentation, including on websites, of syncable authenticator guidelines.

part.name: statement
part.p: Authenticators that enable the use of syncable authentication keys SHOULD provide a user interface (UI) that allows subscribers to view the services for which they have created a syncable authentication key, whether that key has been synced, and where that key has been synced. The UI SHALL NOT expose the authentication key itself.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require manageability of syncable authentication keys by the subscriber.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test to verify the ability of the subscriber to obtain information about their syncable keys, but not the key itself.

part.name: statement
part.p: Federal enterprise authentication keys SHALL be stored in sync fabrics that have achieved Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) [FISMA] moderate protections or equivalent.

part.name: objective
part.p: Require FISMA compliance for federal enterprise authentication keys.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine FISMA certification of sync fabric to verify that it meets provides moderate protection.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to federal enterprise use cases only.

part.name: statement
part.p: Devices (e.g., mobile phones, laptops, tablets) that generate, store, and sync authenticators containing federal enterprise authentication keys SHALL be protected by mobile device management software or other device configuration controls that prevent the syncing or sharing of keys to unauthorized devices or sync fabrics.

part.name: objective
part.p: Restrict choices of sync fabric to those approved by the agency.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine acceptance of authentication using syncable authenticators to verify that authentication requires appropriate device configuration management.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to federal enterprise use cases only.

part.name: statement
part.p: Access to the sync fabric SHALL be controlled by agency-managed accounts (e.g., a central identity and access management solution, platform-based managed account) to maintain federal enterprise control over the authentication key's life cycle.

part.name: objective
part.p: Maintain federal control over authentication keys throughout their life cycle.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine choices of sync fabric approved by the agency to verify that it manages access to the fabric.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Applies to federal enterprise use cases only.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verifiers SHALL indicate that user verification (UV) is preferred and SHALL inspect responses to confirm the value of the UV flag.

part.name: objective
part.p: Prefer syncable authenticators providing multi-factor authentication.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that the value of the UV flag is observed.

part.name: statement
part.p: If the user is not verified, agencies SHALL treat the authenticator as a single-factor cryptographic authenticator.

part.name: objective
part.p: Authentication without user verification is single-factor.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine implementation to verify that authentication without user verification requires an additional password or biometric factor.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHALL evaluate the use cases for syncable authenticators and determine the appropriate access policy decisions that they intend to make based on returned information including flags and attestation.

part.name: objective
part.p: Provide basis for trusting information such as flags received from the authenticator.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine procedures and their basis to determine that appropriate attention has been paid to reliability of information received from syncable authenticators.

part.name: statement
part.p: In order to fulfill the requirements for a given FAL, the federation transaction SHALL meet or exceed all requirements listed for that FAL.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine that the IdP and RP each enforce all requirements associated with the applicable FAL and that every federation transaction meets or exceeds the criteria defined for that FAL.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied when all controls applicable to the asserted FAL are satisfied.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This requirement ensures that the assurance level claimed in a federation transaction reflects the actual technical protections in use. Each FAL defines minimum requirements for audience restriction, replay protection, assertion injection protection, trust agreement establishment, identifier and key establishment, and presentation. Both the IdP and RP must enforce those requirements so that no transaction is represented as operating at a higher FAL than the implemented controls support.
See also SECC-4, which is a summative control for xAL baseline compliance.

part.name: statement
part.p: At all FALs, all federation transactions SHALL comply with the requirements in Sec. 3 to deliver an assertion to the RP and create an authenticated session at the RP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether all federation transactions comply with the requirements in Section 3 for assertion delivery and RP session establishment.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: For IdPs, satisfied by AAD-1, AAD-4, AAD-6, TSI-1, IDA-1 through IDA-3, ARTP-1, ARTI-1, SIGNA-1, SIGNA-3, SIGNA-4, and AUDR-1; also by PROXY-1, PROXY-3 if proxied federation is used; PPI-1, PPI-4 through PPI-8, PPI-10 if PPIs are used; DAV-1 if derived attribute values are used; and ENCA-1 if encrypted assertions are used. If FAL3, satisfied by HKA-1, HKA-3, HKA-5 when HoK assertions are used, and BAUTH-1 when the bound-authenticators are used.

For RPs, satisfied by ASRP-1, SIGNA-2, and AUDR-2; also by FEDID-1, FEDID-2 when federated identifiers are used or ACCR-1 when account resolution is used; ABUN-2 and ABUN-3 if attribute bundles are used; and IDAP-3 if identity APIs are used. If FAL3, satisfied by ASRP-2; also HKA-2, RPPHBA-1, RPPHBA-3, RPPHBA-4 when HoK assertions are used; and BAUTH-5, BAUTH-7, RPPHBA-1, RPPHBA-3, and RPPHBA-4 when the bound-authenticators are used.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This is a summative control based on the outcomes of all controls governing assertion delivery and RP session creation. Compliance is demonstrated when all applicable Section 3 requirements are met.

part.name: statement
part.p: At all FALs, the RP SHALL validate the assertion from the IdP, since the RP needs to trust the IdP to provide valid assertions representing the subscriber's authentication event.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the RP validates each assertion received from the IdP to ensure its authenticity, integrity, and origin before establishing a session.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by ARTC-10 and ARTVL-3.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This is a summative control. Assertion validation is assessed under ARTC-10 (traditional federation) and ARTVL-3 (subscriber-controlled wallets).

part.name: statement
part.p: All parties in the federation SHALL employ security controls, as discussed in Sec. 3.11.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the party undergoing assessment employs the security controls required in Section 3.11.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: For IdPs/CSPs, satisfied by SECC-1, SECC-4, PSI-1 through PSI-3, and SSIN-2.
For RPs, satisfied by SECC-2 through SECC-4, PSI-1 through PSI-3, and SSIN-1 through SSIN-3.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Section 3.11 establishes a tiered security controls baseline for federation participants. CSPs and IdPs must implement appropriately tailored controls from at least the SP 800-53 moderate baseline (or equivalent federal or industry standard such as FedRAMP). RPs must implement at least the low baseline, but RPs that request or process personal information must step up to the moderate baseline. All parties must also satisfy the minimum assurance-related controls for their systems.

This is a summative control that relies on the conclusions of all applicable assessments related to Section 3.11 in this catalog. Compliance is demonstrated when all Section 3.11 requirements applicable to the assessed party are met.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL1, the IdP SHALL sign the assertion using approved cryptography.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether approved cryptography is used for the assertion signature.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the IdP's assertion signing configuration to confirm that all assertions are cryptographically signed using approved algorithms and key sizes.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by generating an assertion from the IdP and verifying the presence of a cryptographic signature using approved cryptography. See SIGNA-4 for assessment of the specific signature mechanism and key type.

part.name: guidance
part.p: SP 800-63-4 defines approved cryptography as any algorithm, hash function, random bit generator, or similar technique that is FIPS-approved or NIST-recommended. For assertion signatures, the relevant standards are FIPS 186-5 (Digital Signature Standard, covering RSA, ECDSA, and EdDSA) and SP 800-131A (algorithm and key length transition schedules). Assessors should verify the IdP's signing algorithm and key size against these references.

part.name: statement
part.p: The RP SHALL validate the signature using the verification key associated with the expected IdP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the RP validates the assertion signature using the verification key associated with the expected IdP.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the RP's signature-validation logic, configuration, and key-establishment documentation to verify that the RP selects the verification key based on the expected IdP identifier and validates assertion signatures only with the verification key associated with that IdP.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the documented results of conformance testing to the IdP/RP implemented standards, protocols, and profiles if available (e.g., OIDC federation OP test)

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by setting up a test IdP and (1) Presenting a valid assertion signed by the expected IdP's key. Verify acceptance. (2) Presenting an assertion signed by a different trusted IdP's valid key. Verify rejection. (3) Presenting an assertion claiming the expected IdP as issuer but signed with a different IdP's key. Verify rejection. (4) Presenting an assertion signed with an unknown or untrusted key. Verify rejection. (5) Presenting an assertion with no signature. Verify rejection.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This requirement ensures that the RP verifies the cryptographic signature on assertions to confirm their authenticity and integrity. The RP must use the verification key specifically associated with the expected IdP. For assessment of how the RP obtains and establishes that key through trusted mechanisms (discovery, registration, manual exchange, or federation authorities), see ICKM-1 and ICKM-2. For assessment of the specific signature mechanism type, see SIGNA-4.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL1, the assertion SHALL be audience-restricted to a specific RP or set of RPs.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the IdP includes audience restrictions in all FAL1 assertions targeting specific RP(s).

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by AUDR-1.

part.name: guidance
part.p: At all FALs, the IdP must include audience restrictions identifying the intended recipient(s). FAL1 allows multiple RPs per assertion, but the assertion must explicitly list all intended recipients. This prevents unscoped assertions that could be accepted by any RP. To reduce the risk of assertion replay, IdPs SHOULD issue assertions designated for a single audience whenever possible. Restriction to a single audience becomes mandatory at FAL2 and higher.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL1, the RP SHALL validate that it is one of the targeted RPs for the given assertion.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that the RP validates each received assertion to ensure its own identifier appears in the audience restriction and rejects any assertion not explicitly targeted to it.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by AUDR-2.

part.name: guidance
part.p: The RP must check that its identifier appears in the assertion's audience field. This prevents replay attacks where assertions intended for other RPs are injected at an unintended RP. If the RP utilizes an IdP that lists multiple RPs in a single assertion at FAL1, confirm that the RP correctly handles assertions containing multiple RP identifiers.

part.name: statement
part.p: Each RP in the [assertion] audience SHALL enforce replay protection mechanisms in the assertion to ensure that the same assertion is not accepted by a given RP multiple times.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that the RP enforces replay protection by detecting and rejecting any assertion that has already been accepted, ensuring the same assertion cannot be used more than once.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine RP documentation, federation configuration, code, and test results to confirm that replay detection mechanisms exist (e.g., nonce validation, assertion ID, and timestamp) and that repeated assertions are rejected.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documented results of conformance testing to the standards, protocols, and profiles implemented by the RP, if available.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test the RP configuration by replaying a previously accepted, valid assertion. Confirm rejection.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Replay protection ensures that a given RP does not accept the same assertion more than once within its validity time window. At FAL1, where multi-audience assertions are permitted, each RP in the audience may accept the assertion once - but no individual RP may accept it a second time. Common replay detection mechanisms include tracking assertion identifiers, validating nonces, and enforcing timestamp-based expiration windows.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL2, the assertion SHALL be strongly protected from assertion injection attacks, as discussed in Sec. 3.11.1.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the RP implements strong protections against assertion injection attacks consistent with Sec. 3.11.1.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by implementing all of the following: FAL1-1, FAL1-2, FAL1-5, FAL2-2, ARTRQ-1, AUDR-1, ARTC-7, ARTC-10 items 3 and 5, AUDR-2, BCP-1 through BCP-10, FCP-1 through FCP-3.

part.name: guidance
part.p: An assertion injection attack in the context of a federated protocol consists of an attacker attempting to force an RP to accept or process an assertion or assertion reference in order to gain access to the RP or deny a legitimate subscriber access to the RP. The attacker does this by taking an assertion or assertion reference and injecting it into a vulnerable RP. A successful attacker can trick an RP into binding the attacker's session to the federated identifier in the assertion. The attacker's assertion could be either stolen from a legitimate subscriber or manufactured to perpetrate the attack.

Protection from assertion injection attacks is recommended at all FALs and required at FAL2 and above. In all cases, the RP needs to take reasonable steps to prevent an attacker from presenting an injected assertion or assertion reference based on the nature of the RP software, the capabilities of the federation protocol in use, and the needs of the overall system.

part.name: statement
part.p: The federation transaction SHALL be initiated by the RP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that, at FAL2 and above, all federation transactions are initiated by the RP rather than the IdP.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the RP's federation implementation and protocol configuration to confirm that all authentication requests originate from the RP. Verify that unsolicited IdP-initiated assertions are not accepted at FAL2 or above.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test the RP flow by delivering an assertion directly to the RP's federation endpoint without initiating the transaction at the RP. Confirm the RP rejects it.

part.name: guidance
part.p: IdP-initiated federation processes are prohibited at FAL2 and FAL3 to prevent the RP from accepting unsolicited assertions and assertion references from the IdP. Inclusion and validation of RP-provided nonces in assertions is an indication of an RP-initiated transaction. However, this prohibition does not include processes in which an external party (e.g., the IdP or a federation authority) signals the RP to start a federation process with the IdP, allowing the RP to begin the federation transaction and securely await a response within that transaction.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL2, the assertion SHALL be audience restricted to a single RP.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that, at FAL2 and above, the IdP includes an audience restriction in each assertion that designates exactly one RP as the intended recipient.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by AUDR-1.

part.name: guidance
part.p: At FAL2, assertions must be explicitly scoped to a single RP to prevent cross-RP assertion replay. Unlike FAL1, where multiple audiences are permitted, FAL2 and above require one-to-one binding between the assertion and the RP, ensuring that a captured assertion cannot be reused at another RP within the federation.

part.name: statement
part.p: The RP SHALL enforce replay protection mechanisms in the assertion.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the RP enforces replay protection mechanisms.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by FAL1-5.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This is the FAL2/FAL3 restatement of the replay protection requirement from Sec. 2.2 (see FAL1-5). At FAL2+, multi-audience assertions are not permitted, so replay protection applies to single-audience assertions only. The assessment methodology and test procedures are the same as FAL1-5.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL2, federated identifiers SHALL NOT contain plaintext personal information, such as usernames, email addresses, employee numbers, etc.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that, at FAL2 and above, the IdP issues federated identifiers that do not include any plaintext personal information such as usernames, email addresses, employee numbers, or other directly identifying data.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the IdP's federated identifier construction rules, documentation, and representative issued identifiers to determine whether any federated identifier contains plaintext personal information, such as usernames, email addresses, employee numbers, names, phone numbers, or similar directly identifying values.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test by generating representative identifiers for sample subscriber accounts and verifying that no identifier reveals plaintext personal information.

part.name: guidance
part.p: At FAL2 and higher, identifiers must be privacy-preserving and non-identifying. This protects subscriber privacy if assertions are intercepted.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL2 [or higher], a trust agreement SHALL be established prior to the federation transaction taking place (i.e., a "pre-established" trust agreement), as discussed in Sec. 4.3.1.

part.name: objective
part.p: Verify that, at FAL2 and above, a trust agreement between the IdP and RP is established and in effect before any federation transaction occurs.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by PETA-1, PETA-2, PETA-3, PETA-4, and PETA-7; additionally satisfied by PETA-6 where shared signaling is used, and by PETA-5 where FAL3 is permitted within the trust agreement.

part.name: guidance
part.p: At FAL2 and above, the IdP and RP must have a trust agreement in place before any federation transaction occurs. The agreement must cover all terms identified in Section 4.3.1, but those terms need not appear in a single document. The required content may be spread across multiple artifacts that, together, establish the technical, operational, and legal basis for trust.

Acceptable artifacts can include binding documents such as contracts, memoranda of understanding, or service agreements, and non-binding but authoritative materials such as CSP practice statements, federation authority agreements, or published federation policies. For example, an IdP may publish a policy describing the assurance levels (xALs) it supports, the security controls it enforces, and the responsibilities of RPs. If the RP documents that it has received and accepted that policy, those terms satisfy the corresponding portion of the trust agreement.

part.name: statement
part.p: IdPs operated by or on behalf of federal agencies that present assertions at FAL2 or higher SHALL protect signing keys used to generate assertions with mechanisms validated at [FIPS140] Level 1 or higher.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the IdP protects assertion-signing keys using cryptographic modules validated at FIPS 140 Level 1 or higher.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine the IdP's federation system documentation and configuration to verify that assertion-signing keys are generated, stored, and used only within a FIPS 140-validated cryptographic module. Confirm that the module appears on the CMVP validation list with a status of Active and is validated at Level 1 or higher.

part.name: guidance
part.p: Assessment is required when: The IdP provides assertions to one or more federal agencies or the IdP is a federal agency.

control.title: RP Verification of Subscriber Authenticator Control

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL3, the RP SHALL verify that the subscriber is in control of an authenticator in addition to the assertion.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the RP verifies subscriber control of an authenticator beyond the assertion at FAL3.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: For holder-of-key assertions, satisfied by HKA-2.
For bound authenticators, satisfied by RPPHBA-1 and RPPHBA-4.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This is a summative control. Compliance is demonstrated when the authenticator control mechanism(s) utilized by the RP have been assessed. At least one of these two mechanisms must be implemented to achieve compliance.

At FAL3, the RP must verify both that it has received a valid assertion from the IdP and that the subscriber controls an authenticator in addition to the assertion. The subscriber-controlled authenticator is either identified in a holder-of-key assertion (see Sec. 3.15) or is an authenticator bound to the RP subscriber account (see Sec. 3.16). In both cases, the authenticator must be phishing-resistant, and the RP must verify proof of control before granting access.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL3, a trust agreement SHALL be established prior to the federation transaction taking place (i.e., a "pre-established" trust agreement), as discussed in Sec. 4.3.1.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether trust agreement artifact(s) are pre-established prior to the federation transaction.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by FAL2-6.

part.name: statement
part.p: At FAL3, the identifiers for the CSP, IdP, and RP SHALL be established manually.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether identifiers for all federation parties are established through manual processes at FAL3.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine configuration documentation to confirm that federation identifiers (e.g., entity IDs, issuer URIs) for the CSP, IdP, and RP are manually configured by authorized personnel. Verify that dynamic registration (Sec. 4.4.2) is not enabled for FAL3 transactions.

part.name: guidance
part.p: FAL3 prohibits dynamic or automated identifier establishment. Party identifiers must be manually configured through direct administrative action. This requirement reduces automated attack vectors and ensures human verification of party identity before establishing FAL3 connections.

part.name: statement
part.p: Each [CSP, IdP, and RP] identifier SHALL be uniquely associated with the verification keys for the party represented.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether each party identifier is uniquely bound to that party's verification keys.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine configuration data or metadata to confirm that each federation participant's identifier (e.g., entity ID) maps to a distinct and authorized verification key or key set. Verify that no key is shared across different identifiers and that key rotation procedures preserve this one-to-one mapping.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This control prevents key-substitution and impersonation attacks by ensuring that when a signature verifies under a stored key, it can only be attributed to the single, specific party whose identifier is bound to that key in the local configuration.

part.name: statement
part.p: Verification keys SHALL be transmitted through a trusted mechanism, which could be manual or automated, as indicated in the trust agreement.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether verification keys are transmitted through a trusted mechanism, ensuring that key material is received from an authenticated and authorized source, and that the mechanism is documented as part of the trust agreement.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Examine documented procedures to determine how verification keys are exchanged, confirming that the mechanism matches the trusted method specified in the relevant trust agreement artifact(s). Determine whether the key exchange mechanism is manual or automated. For automated mechanisms, confirm conformance with ICKM-2. For manual mechanisms, verify that procedures are in place to confirm that the requesting party's identity has been sufficiently verified. Verify that the mechanism for transmitting the verification key is accurately documented and made available to the key recipients.

part.name: guidance
part.p: This requirement ensures that each participant obtains verification keys only from validated sources consistent with the established trust agreement. For example, a public-key certificate that represents the RP is uploaded to the IdP during a manual registration process. The RP is manually configured with a URL that it can use to download the IdP's public key. Alternatively, the IdP and RP could each upload their respective public keys to a federation authority and then download each other's keys from that same location. For a subscriber-controlled wallet, the RP could be manually configured with the URL that represents the CSP's public key. The RP fetches this public key and uses it to validate the signature of the attribute bundle presented by the subscriber-controlled wallet. See Sec. 3.6 for more information on the establishment, management, rotation, and revocation of keys and their association with identifiers.

part.name: statement
part.p: IdPs SHALL support a mechanism for RPs to specify a set of minimum acceptable xALs as part of the trust agreement.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the IdP provides a mechanism for RPs to specify minimum acceptable xALs in the trust agreement.

part.name: assessment-method
part.title: Assessment Method
part.p: Satisfied by PETA-1, item (n).

part.name: guidance
part.p: PETA-1, item (n) requires the trust agreement artifact(s) to document the xALs required by the RPs the IdP supports.

part.name: statement
part.p: The IdP SHALL always indicate the resulting xAL in the assertion, even if the request has not been met.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the IdP includes the actual xAL values achieved in every assertion.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: The presence of xALs in assertions is satisfied by RXAL-3 (IAL), RXAL-4 (AAL), and RXAL-5 (FAL).

Examine the IdP's federation processing logic, assertion-generation logic, configuration, and documentation to determine how the IdP handles transactions in which the RP requests xAL values that the IdP cannot satisfy. Determine whether the IdP issues an assertion containing the xAL values actually achieved, or fails the request and does not issue an assertion.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: Test the IdP using a transaction in which the RP requests xAL values that the IdP cannot satisfy. If the IdP is designed to issue an assertion in that case, determine that the assertion contains the xAL values actually achieved rather than the xAL values requested by the RP. If the IdP is designed to fail the request in that case, determine that the transaction fails and that no assertion is issued.

part.name: guidance
part.p: IdPs must report the actual IAL, AAL, and FAL in the assertion, regardless of what the RP requested. This allows RPs to make informed access decisions when requirements aren't met. For example, if the subscriber has an active session that was authenticated at AAL1, but the RP has requested AAL2, the IdP needs to prompt the subscriber for AAL2 authentication to increase the security of the session at the IdP during the subscriber's interaction at the IdP, if possible. The IdP sends the resulting AAL as part of the returned assertion, whether it is AAL1 (i.e., the step-up authentication request was not met) or AAL2 (i.e., the step-up authentication request was met successfully).

part.name: statement
part.p: The IdP SHALL inform the RP of the following information for each federation transaction: The IAL of the subscriber account being presented to the RP, or an indication that no IAL claim is being made.

part.name: objective
part.p: Determine whether the IdP informs the RP of the IAL for each federation transaction.

part.name: assessment-method
part.p: If the IAL is static: Satisfied by RXAL-6.
